translations.idiomatic: Liu Jizu, Zhai Deng'e, and others; Liu Zuosu, Shen Yanqing, Li Renyuan, Li Fupei, and Wang Enshou

translations.idiomatic: Yu Songshang, Nabuku, Li Huai, Tang Zhi, Zhong Putang, and others; Lin Yuan'en and Tang Desheng

translations.idiomatic: Bi Dayu, Tang Shiquan, Liu Fulin, Xie Zicheng, Zhou Xianzeng, and others; Wen Ying, Xu Fengjie, and others

translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jigong, Fu Shizhen, Qu Jun, Mao Fen, Shi Zuolin, Han Tizhen, and Dekedenge

translations.literal: Jiang Jiagu, Deng Lingyun, Chenshun, Tuokeqing'a, Feng Yuanji
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiagu, Deng Lingyun, Chenshun, Tuokeqing'a, and Feng Yuanji

translations.literal: Ping Yuan, Zhang Baohua, Wang Si, Zhou Laiyu, Yu Baokun, Wang Rukui
translations.idiomatic: Ping Yuan, Zhang Baohua, Wang Si, Zhou Laiyu, Yu Baokun, and Wang Rukui

sentences.zh: 王淑元，字秋查，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Wang Shuyuan, style name Qiucha, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shuyuan, styled Qiucha, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 以舉人知縣，分發廣西。

translations.literal: Having passed the provincial examination, he was appointed district magistrate and dispatched to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: After earning his juren degree, he was appointed district magistrate and sent to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 歷權柳城、雒容、平南、馬平等縣事，授博平，調天保。

translations.literal: He successively served as acting magistrate of Liucheng, Luorong, Pingnan, and Maping counties, was appointed to Boping, then transferred to Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as acting magistrate of Liucheng, Luorong, Pingnan, and Maping, then received a regular appointment at Boping before being transferred to Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 會臨桂縣民以糧價重不輸稅，大吏欲懾以兵，淑元在省，進議曰：「民固有所苦，得平自服。」

translations.literal: When the people of Lingui County refused to pay taxes because grain prices were high, senior officials wished to intimidate them with troops. Shuyuan was in the provincial capital and submitted a recommendation, saying: "The people indeed have grievances; if matters are made fair, they will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Lingui County stopped paying taxes because grain prices were too high, senior officials wanted to cow them with force. Shuyuan was at the provincial capital and advised: "The people truly have grievances; set things right and they will comply on their own."

sentences.zh: 遂調臨桂。

translations.literal: He was therefore transferred to Lingui.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly transferred to Lingui.

sentences.zh: 既蒞任，為汰浮收，民便之，無逋賦者。

translations.literal: Once he took office, he eliminated excessive collections, which benefited the people, and there were no arrears in tax payments.
translations.idiomatic: After he assumed office, he cut out illegal surcharges, greatly easing the burden on the people, and tax arrears disappeared.

sentences.zh: 道光季年，粵匪洪秀全始謀逆，其黨李嘉耀潛入省垣煽土匪內應，發覺，淑元鞫得餘匪匿所，悉數掩擒，敘功昇龍州同知，以肅清會匪獎知府銜。

translations.literal: In the last years of the Daoguang reign, the Guangdong bandit Hong Xiuquan first plotted rebellion. His follower Li Jiayao secretly entered the provincial capital to incite local bandits as internal collaborators. When this was discovered, Shuyuan interrogated and learned the hiding places of the remaining bandits, captured them all in raids, and for this merit was promoted to subprefect of Longzhou and awarded the rank of prefect for clearing out secret-society bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of Daoguang, the Guangdong rebel Hong Xiuquan first began plotting insurrection. His associate Li Jiayao slipped into the provincial capital to stir up local bandits as inside collaborators. Once the plot was exposed, Shuyuan interrogated his prisoners, tracked down the remaining bandits' hideouts, and captured them all. For this he was promoted to subprefect of Longzhou and granted the honorary rank of prefect for suppressing secret-society bandits.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，擢太平府知府，旋任龍州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, he was promoted to prefect of Taiping Prefecture, and soon afterward was assigned to Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to prefect of Taiping Prefecture, and soon after took charge of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 時廣西巡撫鄭祖琛懦而黯，群盜蜂起，輒務諱匿。

translations.literal: At that time the Guangxi governor Zheng Zuchen was cowardly and corrupt; bandits rose everywhere like bees, yet he constantly sought to conceal the reports.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangxi governor Zheng Zuchen was timid and corrupt; bandits swarmed across the province, yet he habitually covered up every report.

sentences.zh: 三十年，賊潘寶源等來犯，淑元率練丁禦諸距州十里之灣道，以次子光頡自隨。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the bandits Pan Baoyuan and others came to attack. Shuyuan led militia to resist them at Wandao, ten li from the prefectural seat, taking his second son Guangjie with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year the bandits Pan Baoyuan and others attacked. Shuyuan led his militia to meet them at Wandao, ten li from the prefectural seat, bringing his second son Guangjie with him.

sentences.zh: 戰不利，雨甚，藥濕砲不及發，因退回城。

translations.literal: The battle went poorly; the rain was heavy and the gunpowder damp so the cannon could not be fired, and they therefore retreated to the city.
translations.idiomatic: The fight went badly. Heavy rain soaked the gunpowder and the cannon could not be fired, so they fell back toward the city.

sentences.zh: 及門，賊已由間道入，擁眾逼官廨。

translations.literal: When they reached the gate, the bandits had already entered by a hidden path and pressed the yamen with their masses.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached the gate, the bandits had already entered by a back route and were pressing the yamen in force.

sentences.zh: 淑元立堂上，罵不絕口，呼家眾殺賊。

translations.literal: Shuyuan stood in the main hall, cursing without pause, and called on his household to kill the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyuan stood in the main hall, cursing without cease, and called on his household to kill the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊斫淑元僕地，擄之去，光頡奔奪，賊殺光頡，而投淑元於勤村河。

translations.literal: The bandits cut Shuyuan down and he fell; they carried him off. Guangjie rushed forward to rescue him; the bandits killed Guangjie and threw Shuyuan into the Qincun River.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits struck Shuyuan down and dragged him away. Guangjie ran forward to rescue him; the bandits killed Guangjie and threw Shuyuan into the Qincun River.

sentences.zh: 盜去三日，始出之，身首皆裂，獨面色如生。

translations.literal: Three days after the bandits left, the body was retrieved; head and body were both severed, yet his face was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after the bandits departed, the body was recovered. Head and trunk were both mangled, yet his face looked as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 高延祉，字筠坡，浙江蕭山人。

translations.literal: Gao Yanzhi, style name Yunpo, was a native of Xiaoshan County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanzhi, styled Yunpo, was a native of Xiaoshan County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 由舉人充官學教習，期滿，用知縣。

translations.literal: As a provincial graduate he served as an instructor in the Imperial Academy; when his term expired, he was appointed district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examination, he served as an instructor at the Imperial Academy; when his term ended, he was appointed district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 道光二十一年，英夷犯浙江沿海，舉行團練，延祉率義勇為前驅，擊毀夷船。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, when the English barbarians attacked the Zhejiang coast, local militia were organized. Yanzhi led the volunteer forces as vanguard and struck and destroyed enemy ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Daoguang, when British forces attacked the Zhejiang coast, local militia were mobilized. Yanzhi led the volunteers as vanguard and destroyed enemy vessels.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，揀發廣西，與都下親友別，即以致身奉國自誓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was selected for service in Guangxi. When he parted from relatives and friends in the capital, he vowed at once to devote his life to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was selected for assignment to Guangxi. As he bid farewell to friends and kin in the capital, he pledged himself to the service of the state.

sentences.zh: 尋署隆安縣事，土賊陸鵬理與其黨乃利中、凌阿東等，屢為邑害。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as acting magistrate of Long'an County. The local bandits Lu Pengli and his followers Nai Lizhong, Ling Adong, and others repeatedly plagued the district.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took charge of Long'an County, where the local bandits Lu Pengli and his followers Nai Lizhong, Ling Adong, and others had long been a scourge.

sentences.zh: 延祉集團練，遣間諜，以計誘殺鵬理，捕獲其家屬黨與二十餘人，並毀利中巢窟及塚。

translations.literal: Yanzhi gathered the militia, sent spies, and by stratagem lured and killed Pengli. He captured more than twenty of his family members and followers, and also destroyed Lizhong's lair and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi assembled the militia, sent out spies, and by a ruse lured Pengli to his death. He captured more than twenty of Pengli's kin and followers and destroyed Lizhong's stronghold and tomb.

sentences.zh: 阿東亡命，謀復仇，糾眾千餘，據白山之感墟，與歸德接壤。

translations.literal: Adong fled as an outlaw and plotted revenge, gathering more than a thousand men and occupying Ganxu on Mount Baishan, bordering Guide.
translations.idiomatic: Adong went into hiding and plotted revenge, mustering more than a thousand men and seizing Ganxu on Mount Baishan, on the border with Guide.

sentences.zh: 延祉偕歸德土知州黃為錦率練勇四百進攻，沿途搜戮賊探多名，行抵袍墟，距感墟十餘裡，遇伏，軍潰。

translations.literal: Yanzhi together with Huang Weijin, the native-subject magistrate of Guide, led four hundred militiamen in an attack. Along the way they hunted down and killed many bandit scouts. When they reached Paoxu, more than ten li from Ganxu, they met an ambush and the force collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi joined Huang Weijin, the native-subject magistrate of Guide, in leading four hundred militiamen against them. En route they killed many bandit scouts. At Paoxu, a little over ten li from Ganxu, they walked into an ambush and the column broke.

sentences.zh: 复激勵練勇奮擊，殪匪二百餘。

translations.literal: He again roused the militia to fight fiercely and killed more than two hundred bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the militia to fight on and killed more than two hundred bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊眾蜂至，延祉挺刃督戰，被賊矛中腹遇害，為錦亦戰死，僕隸多殉之者。

translations.literal: Bandits swarmed in. Yanzhi drew his blade and directed the fighting; he was struck in the abdomen by a bandit spear and killed. Weijin also died in battle, and many of their servants died with them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits poured in from every side. Yanzhi drew his sword and led the fight, but a bandit spear pierced his belly and killed him. Weijin also fell in battle, and many of their attendants died with them.

sentences.zh: 延祉任隆安七十餘日，無日不在外治戰事，居縣廨僅數日耳。

translations.literal: During more than seventy days as magistrate of Long'an, Yanzhi spent not a single day without being abroad handling military affairs; he lived in the county yamen for only a few days.
translations.idiomatic: In his seventy-odd days at Long'an, Yanzhi was in the field every day and spent only a few nights in the county yamen.

sentences.zh: 民感其保衛之恩，爭賻其孤，孤；

translations.literal: The people, grateful for his protection, vied to give gifts to his orphan; orphan;
translations.idiomatic: The people, grateful for his protection, vied to contribute to his orphaned son;

sentences.zh: 乃以其貲建祠祀之，以從死之僕隸、壯勇附。

translations.literal: They therefore used these funds to build a shrine in his honor, with the servants and militiamen who died with him enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: With those gifts they built a shrine in his honor, enshrining alongside him the servants and militiamen who had died with him.

sentences.zh: 同治十一年，追諡壯節。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he was posthumously granted the honorific Zhuangjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tongzhi he was posthumously granted the honorific title Zhuangjie, "Steadfast Integrity."

sentences.zh: 為錦，山東人。

translations.literal: Weijin was a native of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Weijin was from Shandong.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟，白氏，漢軍鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Ruilin, of the Bai clan, was a member of the Han Chinese Bordered White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ruilin, of the Bai clan, belonged to the Han Chinese Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 由謄錄議敘巡檢，道光五年，選廣西鎮峽寨巡檢。

translations.literal: Through service as a copyist he earned appointment as an assistant magistrate. In the fifth year of Daoguang he was selected as assistant magistrate of Zhenxia Stockade in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Through service as a copyist he earned appointment as an assistant magistrate, and in the fifth year of Daoguang was posted to Zhenxia Stockade in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 調主簿，擢州判、知州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk, then promoted to subprefect and prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief clerk, then promoted through subprefect to prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，授西隆州知州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Xilong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Xilong.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年二月，洪秀全自永安犯桂林，敗竄全州，瑞麟已卸州事，繼任知州曹燮培知瑞麟才，深相結納，約共守禦。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Xianfeng, Hong Xiuquan marched from Yong'an against Guilin, was defeated, and fled to Quanzhou. Ruilin had already relinquished his prefectural duties, but his successor Cao Xiepei, recognizing Ruilin's talent, formed a close bond with him and agreed to defend the city together.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Xianfeng, Hong Xiuquan marched from Yong'an against Guilin, was beaten back, and fled toward Quanzhou. Ruilin had already left office, but his successor Cao Xiepei, recognizing his ability, drew him close and pledged to defend the city together.

sentences.zh: 時都司武昌顯以楚兵四百援桂林，道經全州，燮培留助守。

translations.literal: At that time the battalion commander Wu Changxian was bringing four hundred Chu troops to relieve Guilin. Passing through Quanzhou, Xiepei retained him to help defend the city.
translations.idiomatic: The battalion commander Wu Changxian was then marching four hundred Hunan troops to relieve Guilin. Passing through Quanzhou, Xiepei kept him to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊薄城下，發砲轟擊，斃賊甚夥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the bandits pressed close to the city walls. Cannon fire was unleashed and many bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels closed on the walls. Cannon fire tore into them and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 越日攻益急，歷十一晝夜，提督餘萬清、劉長清來援，分駐城北太平堡，城西魯班橋，距十五里外，牽制弗能進，守者憊甚，子藥不繼。

translations.literal: The next day the attack grew fiercer and continued for eleven days and nights. The provincial commanders Yu Wanqing and Liu Changqing came to relieve the city, but stationed separately at Taiping Fort north of the city and Luban Bridge west of the city, fifteen li away, and could not advance because they were held in check. The defenders were exhausted and ammunition ran short.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the assault intensified and raged for eleven days and nights. Provincial commanders Yu Wanqing and Liu Changqing arrived to relieve the city but halted fifteen li away, at Taiping Fort to the north and Luban Bridge to the west, unable to break through. The defenders were exhausted and ammunition was running out.

sentences.zh: 賊穴城，地雷發，城崩，賊乘入，千總葉永林、把總張元福死之。

translations.literal: The bandits tunneled under the wall; a land mine detonated, the wall collapsed, and the bandits rushed in. The company commanders Ye Yonglin and Zhang Yuanfu were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels mined beneath the wall. When the charge blew, the wall collapsed and they poured in. Company commanders Ye Yonglin and Zhang Yuanfu were killed.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟素驍勇，遇賊中衢，手刃數人，力竭身死。

translations.literal: Ruilin had always been bold in battle. He met the bandits in the middle of the street, killed several with his own hand, and died when his strength was spent.
translations.idiomatic: Ruilin had always been a fierce fighter. He met the rebels in the street, cut down several with his own hand, and fell when his strength gave out.

sentences.zh: 燮培亦巷戰死。

translations.literal: Xiepei also died fighting in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Xiepei also died fighting in the alleys.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城時，多死傷，恨甚，城陷，屠之，焚屋舍幾盡。

translations.literal: During the siege the bandits had suffered many casualties and hated the city deeply. When it fell they massacred the population and burned nearly all the buildings.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had taken heavy losses during the siege and nursed a deep grudge. When the city fell they slaughtered the people and burned nearly every building.

sentences.zh: 文武官紳同時死者：署全州營參將楊映河，把總卜有祥，解餉官四川知縣盧金第，安徽府經歷陳堯，湖南游擊餘遇升，都司武昌顯，千總田慶華、馬瑞龍，把總盧先振、黃志林、韓大興，外委孫紹全、楊清麒、田宏義、楊大賓、龔心仁、田宗南，武舉唐殿試，生員蔣成龍、金建勳，武生張以敬，幕友黃柏彬、祝永文、硃福坪、周希齡、孫培駒、楊菱舟、金家駒、硃澤，凡三十餘人。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials and gentry who died at the same time included: the acting brigade commander of Quanzhou garrison Yang Yinghe; platoon commander Bu Youxiang; the grain-transport official, Sichuan district magistrate Lu Jindi; Anhui prefectural secretary Chen Yao; Hunan regimental commander Yu Yusheng; battalion commander Wu Changxian; company commanders Tian Qinghua and Ma Ruilong; platoon commanders Lu Xianzhen, Huang Zhilin, and Han Daxing; junior officers Sun Shaoquan, Yang Qingqi, Tian Hongyi, Yang Dabin, Gong Xinren, and Tian Zongnan; military licentiate Tang Dianshi; licentiate degree holders Jiang Chenglong and Jin Jianxun; military licentiate Zhang Yijing; and secretaries Huang Baibin, Zhu Yongwen, Zhu Fuping, Zhou Xiling, Sun Peiju, Yang Lingzhou, Jin Jiuju, and Zhu Ze—in all more than thirty persons.
translations.idiomatic: Among the civil and military officials and local gentry who fell at the same time were the acting brigade commander of the Quanzhou garrison, Yang Yinghe; platoon commander Bu Youxiang; grain-transport official and Sichuan district magistrate Lu Jindi; Anhui prefectural secretary Chen Yao; Hunan regimental commander Yu Yusheng; battalion commander Wu Changxian; company commanders Tian Qinghua and Ma Ruilong; platoon commanders Lu Xianzhen, Huang Zhilin, and Han Daxing; junior officers Sun Shaoquan, Yang Qingqi, Tian Hongyi, Yang Dabin, Gong Xinren, and Tian Zongnan; military licentiate Tang Dianshi; licentiates Jiang Chenglong and Jin Jianxun; military licentiate Zhang Yijing; and secretaries Huang Baibin, Zhu Yongwen, Zhu Fuping, Zhou Xiling, Sun Peiju, Yang Lingzhou, Jin Jiuju, and Zhu Ze—more than thirty in all.

sentences.zh: 學正農賢託，年七十，甫歿，棺毀，妻殉之。

translations.literal: The director of studies Nong Xiantuo, aged seventy, had just died; his coffin was destroyed, and his wife died with him.
translations.idiomatic: The director of studies Nong Xiantuo, seventy years old, had only just died; the rebels smashed his coffin, and his wife died with him.

sentences.zh: 瑞麟諡壯節，與燮培並贈道銜，詔祀京師昭忠祠。

translations.literal: Ruilin was posthumously granted the honorific Zhuangjie; he and Xiepei were both awarded the rank of circuit intendant, and an edict ordered them enshrined in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ruilin was posthumously granted the title Zhuangjie; he and Xiepei were both awarded the honorary rank of circuit intendant, and an edict ordered their enshrinement in the Capital Shrine of Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建專祠全州，曰愍忠，祀燮培及諸死事者。

translations.literal: A dedicated shrine called Minzhong was built at Quanzhou to honor Xiepei and all who died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: A dedicated shrine called Minzhong, "Commemorating the Loyal," was built at Quanzhou to honor Xiepei and all who died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 燮培，字理村，浙江仁和人。

translations.literal: Xiepei, style name Licun, was a native of Renhe County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xiepei, styled Licun, was a native of Renhe County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 選柳州通判，攝西隆州、賓州事，除東蘭州知州，權全州。

translations.literal: He was selected as subprefect of Liuzhou, served as acting prefect of Xilong and Bin Prefectures, was appointed prefect of Donglan Prefecture, and held Quanzhou in an acting capacity.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as subprefect of Liuzhou, served as acting prefect of Xilong and Bin, was appointed prefect of Donglan, and held Quanzhou in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻，有吏才，不拘節目，聲伎滿前，然無廢事。

translations.literal: By nature he was free-spirited and possessed administrative talent. He did not bind himself to formal rules; singers and performers filled his hall, yet no official business went neglected.
translations.idiomatic: Free-spirited and capable in office, he cared little for formal propriety. Singers and entertainers filled his hall, yet no official business was neglected.

sentences.zh: 或規之，引文信國公少年時事自解，曰：「他日能學文山足矣！」

translations.literal: When someone admonished him, he cited the youthful conduct of Duke Wen of Xinguo in his own defense, saying: "If someday I can emulate Wenshan, that will be enough!"
translations.idiomatic: When someone remonstrated with him, he cited the youthful conduct of Duke Wen of Xinguo in his own defense, saying: "If someday I can live up to Wenshan, that will be enough!"

sentences.zh: 人謂燮培無負素志雲。

translations.literal: People said that Xiepei did not betray his lifelong aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: People said Xiepei had not fallen short of the pledge he had made.

sentences.zh: 時死廣西者，又有署永安州吳江龍門司巡檢馮元等。

translations.literal: At that time others who died in Guangxi included Feng Yuan and others, the acting assistant magistrate of Longmen Station in Yong'an Prefecture on the Wujiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died in Guangxi at this time included Feng Yuan, acting assistant magistrate of Longmen Station in Yong'an Prefecture on the Wujiang River, and others.

sentences.zh: 劉繼祖，江西玉山人。

translations.literal: Liu Jizu was a native of Yushan County, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jizu was a native of Yushan County in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 增貢生。

translations.literal: He was an augmented tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of augmented tribute student.

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，以同知分福建。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was appointed subprefect and dispatched to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was appointed subprefect and sent to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 十九年，除淡水同知，以憂去。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed subprefect of Tamsui and left office on account of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed subprefect of Tamsui, then left office to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，借揀知州，發廣西。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he borrowed selection as prefect and was dispatched to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he entered the selection pool for prefect and was sent to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，授永康，尋署藤縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed to Yongkang and soon afterward served as acting magistrate of Teng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year he received Yongkang and soon took charge of Teng County in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 時灌陽、平樂、陽朔等處匪徒肆擾，偕知府張熙宇督剿，殲擒殆盡，進知府。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were rampaging in Guanyang, Pingle, Yangshuo, and other places. Together with the prefect Zhang Xiyu he directed the suppression, nearly exterminating or capturing them all, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were then ravaging Guanyang, Pingle, Yangshuo, and neighboring districts. Working with Prefect Zhang Xiyu, he led the suppression and killed or captured nearly all of them, earning promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，金田賊敗竄大黃江，繼祖率水陸壯勇乘夜攻擊，焚其巢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Jintian bandits, defeated, fled to the Dahuang River. Jizu led land and water militia in a night attack and burned their lair.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng the Jintian rebels, beaten back, fled to the Dahuang River. Jizu led land and river militia in a night assault and burned their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 以所部練勇失鈐束，奪職。

translations.literal: Because the militia under his command had lost discipline, he was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Because the militia under his command had gotten out of hand, he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 四年，巡撫勞崇光奏請留藤協辦團練，尋艇賊梁培友糾眾攻藤，繼祖偕知縣翟登峨等嬰城固守，設間出奇擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the governor Lao Chongguang memorialized asking that he be retained at Teng to assist in organizing the militia. Soon the boat bandits under Liang Peiyou gathered a force and attacked Teng. Jizu together with the district magistrate Zhai Deng'e and others held the city in a tight defense and by stratagem launched a surprise attack that drove the bandits back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Governor Lao Chongguang asked that he be kept at Teng to help organize the militia. Soon the boat bandit Liang Peiyou mustered a force and attacked the county. Jizu joined District Magistrate Zhai Deng'e and others in a desperate defense and, by a stratagem, launched a surprise attack that drove the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 旋以土賊馮六、戴九等接踵至，據河干，盡焚沿岸舟，鄉團來援者不得渡。

translations.literal: Soon local bandits Feng Liu, Dai Jiu, and others arrived in succession, seized the riverbank, burned all boats along the shore, and prevented militia reinforcements from crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits Feng Liu, Dai Jiu, and others then arrived in turn, seized the riverbank, burned every boat along the shore, and cut off militia reinforcements trying to cross.

sentences.zh: 賊眾兵單，城陷，繼祖受重創，與登峨子襄採、團長梁文軾等巷戰，力竭，死之。

translations.literal: The bandits were many and the defenders few; the city fell. Jizu received grave wounds and, together with Deng'e's son Xiangcai and the militia captain Liang Wenshi and others, fought in the lanes until his strength was spent and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outnumbered the defenders and the city fell. Jizu was gravely wounded and, with Deng'e's son Xiangcai and militia captain Liang Wenshi and others, fought through the alleys until he was spent and killed.

sentences.zh: 登峨被擄，罵賊不屈，被害，棄屍於河。

translations.literal: Deng'e was captured; he cursed the bandits and would not submit, was killed, and his body was thrown into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Deng'e was taken captive. He cursed the rebels and refused to yield; they killed him and threw his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 典史冉正棠鬥死獄門。

translations.literal: The jail superintendent Ran Zhengtang died fighting at the prison gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jail superintendent Ran Zhengtang died fighting at the prison gate.

sentences.zh: 詔复繼祖原官，賞世職，登峨以次死者卹有差。

translations.literal: An edict restored Jizu to his former office and granted hereditary rank; Deng'e and the others who died received posthumous honors according to their stations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Jizu to his former rank and granted hereditary honors; Deng'e and the others who fell received posthumous awards according to their stations.

sentences.zh: 登峨，字眉峰，山東章丘人。

translations.literal: Deng'e, style name Meifeng, was a native of Zhangqiu County, Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Deng'e, styled Meifeng, was a native of Zhangqiu County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 進士，截取選藤縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi degree holder, he was selected by special appointment as magistrate of Teng County.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he was selected by special appointment as magistrate of Teng County.

sentences.zh: 劉作肅，字敬亭，奉天承德縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Zuosu, style name Jingting, was a native of Chengde County, Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zuosu, styled Jingting, was a native of Chengde County in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人，選知縣，授天河縣。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of the first year of Daoguang, he was selected as district magistrate and appointed to Tianhe County.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of the first year of Daoguang, he was selected as district magistrate and appointed to Tianhe County.

sentences.zh: 歷寧明知州，兼明江同知。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Ningming and concurrently as subprefect of Mingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Ningming and concurrently as subprefect of Mingjiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，賊眾萬餘攻城，相持五月餘，解圍去。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng more than ten thousand bandits besieged the city. After a standoff of more than five months they lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng more than ten thousand rebels besieged the city. After more than five months of stalemate they broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以城守功加知府，賞花翎。

translations.literal: For his merit in defending the city he was promoted to prefect and awarded a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For defending the city he was promoted to prefect and awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 六年，署太平知府，賊屢來犯，禦卻之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as acting prefect of Taiping; bandits repeatedly came to attack and he drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as acting prefect of Taiping and repeatedly beat back rebel attacks.

sentences.zh: 十年，復來。

translations.literal: In the tenth year they came again.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year they came again.

sentences.zh: 城中無儲粟，賊圍亟，守陴者皆走。

translations.literal: The city had no stored grain; the siege was pressing; and the men defending the walls all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city had no grain in store, the siege closed in, and the men on the walls fled.

sentences.zh: 城陷，作肅投池，水淺，不能死，為賊擁去。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zuosu threw himself into a pond, but the water was shallow and he could not die; the bandits seized him and carried him off.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zuosu threw himself into a pond, but the water was too shallow to drown him and the rebels dragged him away.

sentences.zh: 以其居官清廉，不忍害之。

translations.literal: Because he had been incorruptible in office, they could not bear to harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had governed with integrity, they could not bring themselves to kill him.

sentences.zh: 作肅乃吟絕命辭，絕粒死。

translations.literal: Zuosu then recited a death poem and died by refusing food.
translations.idiomatic: Zuosu then composed a final poem and starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 其弟與僕姚云、吳貴同殉。

translations.literal: His younger brother and his servants Yao Yun and Wu Gui died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother and his servants Yao Yun and Wu Gui died with him.

sentences.zh: 妻趙及子家祥、女等皆先自盡。

translations.literal: His wife Zhao, his son Jiaxiang, his daughters, and others had all taken their own lives beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Zhao, his son Jiaxiang, his daughters, and others had already killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 以子家鳳被執不屈死，卹如製。

translations.literal: Because his son Jiafeng was captured and died rather than submit, posthumous honors were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Because his son Jiafeng was captured and died rather than submit, the family received posthumous honors according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 賞世職，建祠府城，二僕並賜卹。

translations.literal: Hereditary rank was awarded, a shrine was built in the prefectural city, and the two servants were also granted posthumous honors.
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary honors were granted, a shrine was built in the prefectural city, and the two servants received posthumous awards as well.

sentences.zh: 沈衍慶，字槐卿，安徽石埭人。

translations.literal: Shen Yanqing, style name Huaiqing, was a native of Shidi County, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanqing, styled Huaiqing, was a native of Shidi County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，以知縣發江西，署興國，補泰和。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Daoguang, he was dispatched to Jiangxi as district magistrate, served as acting magistrate of Xingguo, and was appointed to Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Daoguang, he was sent to Jiangxi as district magistrate, served as acting magistrate of Xingguo, and was appointed to Taihe.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，調鄱陽，縣濱湖，盜賊所出沒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Poyang. The county bordered the lake and was a haunt of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to Poyang, a lakeside county where bandits came and went.

sentences.zh: 衍慶編漁戶，仿保甲法行之，屢獲劇盜。

translations.literal: Yanqing organized the fishing households and applied the baojia system, repeatedly capturing major bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing registered the fishing households and applied the baojia system, repeatedly capturing major bandits.

sentences.zh: 俗悍好鬥，輒輕騎馳往，竭誠開導，事浸息。

translations.literal: The local custom was fierce and quarrelsome. He would often ride out lightly armed, earnestly instruct the people, and gradually the troubles subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce and quick to fight. He would ride out lightly armed, earnestly counsel them, and gradually the violence subsided.

sentences.zh: 兩遇水災，盡力賑撫，存活無算。

translations.literal: Twice when flood disasters struck, he exerted himself fully in relief and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: When floods struck twice, he threw himself into relief work and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異。

translations.literal: He was recommended as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended as an outstanding official.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪陷湖北武昌，衍慶請兵守康山，控鄱陽門戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng the Guangdong bandits captured Wuchang in Hubei. Yanqing requested troops to hold Kangshan and guard the gateway to Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng the Guangdong rebels took Wuchang in Hubei. Yanqing asked for troops to hold Kangshan and guard the gateway to Poyang.

sentences.zh: 三年，九江陷，譌言四起，居民逃亡，不可禁止。

translations.literal: In the third year Jiujiang fell; false rumors spread everywhere; residents fled and could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jiujiang fell. Rumors spread in every direction, residents fled, and nothing could stop the panic.

sentences.zh: 衍慶率練勇巡東門，見糧船中數百人譟而前，衍慶手刃二人，餘黨慴服，人心始定。

translations.literal: Yanqing led militia to patrol the east gate and saw several hundred men in grain boats shouting and pressing forward. Yanqing killed two with his own hand; the rest were cowed into submission, and public sentiment finally settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing led militia to patrol the east gate and saw several hundred men in grain boats surging forward in uproar. He cut down two with his own hand; the rest submitted in fear, and the people's minds at last steadied.

sentences.zh: 賊圍南昌，巡撫張芾檄衍慶赴援，會合省防諸軍與賊戰，大破之。

translations.literal: When bandits besieged Nanchang, Governor Zhang Fu ordered Yanqing to go to the relief. He joined the provincial defense forces in battle and routed the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels besieged Nanchang, Governor Zhang Fu ordered Yanqing to the relief. He joined the provincial defense forces, fought the rebels, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊將東竄，衍慶慮賊犯鄱陽，請於巡撫，馳歸。

translations.literal: The bandits were about to flee east. Yanqing feared they would strike Poyang, asked leave of the governor, and raced back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were about to flee east. Fearing they would strike Poyang, Yanqing asked the governor's leave and raced home.

sentences.zh: 時樂平令李仁元攝鄱陽事，同商守禦。

translations.literal: At that time the magistrate of Leping, Li Renyuan, was acting in Poyang affairs and consulted with Yanqing on the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Leping, Li Renyuan, was then acting in Poyang and consulted with Yanqing on the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊至，與仁元同力戰，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived, he fought alongside Renyuan with all his strength. The city fell and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, he fought alongside Renyuan with all his strength. The city fell and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈道銜，立祠鄱陽。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded the rank of circuit intendant, and a shrine was built for him at Poyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the honorary rank of circuit intendant, and a shrine was built for him at Poyang.

sentences.zh: 仁元，字資齋，河南濟源人。

translations.literal: Renyuan, style name Zizhai, was a native of Jiyuan County, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan, styled Zizhai, was a native of Jiyuan County in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，內閣中書，改知縣。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, he served as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat and then transferred to district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, he served as a secretary in the Grand Secretariat before transferring to district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，授樂平。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed to Leping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed magistrate of Leping.

sentences.zh: 民俗剽悍，以禮讓教之，多感悟。

translations.literal: The local custom was fierce and violent; he taught them through ritual and deference, and many were moved to reform.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce by custom; he taught them through ritual and deference, and many were moved to reform.

sentences.zh: 有素習械鬥者，仁元曰：「民不畏死，然後可以致死。

translations.literal: There were men long accustomed to armed brawling. Renyuan said: "When the people do not fear death, then they can be made to face death.
translations.idiomatic: Some were long accustomed to armed brawling. Renyuan said: "When men do not fear death, they can be sent to face it.

sentences.zh: 今天下多事，正此輩效順之時也。」

translations.literal: Now the realm is troubled on every side; this is precisely the time for such men to prove their loyalty."
translations.idiomatic: The realm is troubled on every side; this is precisely the time for such men to prove their loyalty."

sentences.zh: 簡驍健得六百人，日加訓練，土匪畏之，斂跡。

translations.literal: He selected six hundred bold and able men and trained them daily. Local bandits feared them and kept out of sight.
translations.idiomatic: He picked six hundred bold and able men and drilled them daily. Local bandits feared them and kept out of sight.

sentences.zh: 樂平與鄱陽為鄰境，仁元政聲亦與衍慶相埒，至是南昌戒嚴，衍慶助剿，仁元移攝鄱陽以代之。

translations.literal: Leping bordered Poyang, and Renyuan's reputation in office matched Yanqing's. At this time Nanchang was on alert; Yanqing went to assist in the suppression, and Renyuan moved to act in Poyang in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Leping bordered Poyang, and Renyuan's reputation matched Yanqing's. When Nanchang went on alert and Yanqing went to assist in the suppression, Renyuan moved to act in Poyang in his stead.

sentences.zh: 未幾，衍慶以防賊擾，馳歸縣。

translations.literal: Before long Yanqing, fearing bandit raids, raced back to the county.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yanqing, fearing rebel raids, raced back to the county.

sentences.zh: 因仁元父母妻子在樂平，亟趣仁元去。

translations.literal: Because Renyuan's parents, wife, and children were in Leping, he urgently urged Renyuan to go.
translations.idiomatic: Because Renyuan's parents, wife, and children were in Leping, he urgently urged him to leave.

sentences.zh: 仁元曰：「賊旦夕且至，臨敵易令，是謂我不丈夫也。」

translations.literal: Renyuan said: "The bandits will arrive at any moment. To change command on the eve of battle would mean I am no true man."
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan said: "The rebels will arrive at any moment. To change command on the eve of battle would mean I am no true man."

sentences.zh: 遂議並力戰守。

translations.literal: They therefore agreed to fight and defend together.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore agreed to fight and defend together.

sentences.zh: 值久雨湖漲，城圮，無險可攖。

translations.literal: Prolonged rain had swollen the lake; the wall had collapsed, and there was no strongpoint left to hold.
translations.idiomatic: Prolonged rain had swollen the lake, the wall had collapsed, and there was no strongpoint left to hold.

sentences.zh: 於是審度地勢，衍慶軍南門，仁元軍北門，為犄角。

translations.literal: They therefore surveyed the terrain: Yanqing's force at the south gate and Renyuan's at the north gate, forming pincers.
translations.idiomatic: They surveyed the terrain and deployed Yanqing's force at the south gate and Renyuan's at the north gate, forming pincers.

sentences.zh: 部署甫定，賊揚帆大至。

translations.literal: Their deployment had just been set when the bandits arrived under full sail.
translations.idiomatic: Their deployment had barely been set when the rebels arrived under full sail.

sentences.zh: 麾軍燃砲，碎賊艦，賊繞東門登岸，入城，衍慶迎擊，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: He ordered the troops to fire cannon and smash the bandit vessels. The bandits rounded to the east gate, landed, and entered the city. Yanqing met them in counterattack and the bandits fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the troops to fire cannon and smash the rebel vessels. The rebels rounded to the east gate, landed, and entered the city. Yanqing met them in counterattack and drove them back slightly.

sentences.zh: 又繞而北，仁元率樂平勇巷戰，矛刺仁元，踣，臠割之。

translations.literal: They swung north again. Renyuan led the Leping militia in lane fighting; a spear struck Renyuan and he fell; they hacked his body to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: They swung north again. Renyuan led the Leping militia in lane fighting; a spear struck him down and they hacked his body to pieces.

sentences.zh: 所部猶力戰，死者過半，卒得仁元屍以出。

translations.literal: His men still fought fiercely; more than half were killed, but in the end they recovered Renyuan's body and brought it out.
translations.idiomatic: His men still fought on; more than half were killed, but in the end they recovered Renyuan's body and brought it out.

sentences.zh: 初，樂平土匪度仁元去必復來，伏不敢動。

translations.literal: Earlier, the bandits of Leping had assumed Renyuan would certainly return and lay low, not daring to stir.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the bandits of Leping had assumed Renyuan would certainly return and had lain low, not daring to stir.

sentences.zh: 及聞殉難，乃倡議迎賊。

translations.literal: When they heard he had died in the defense, they then proposed welcoming the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard he had died in the defense, they proposed welcoming the rebels.

sentences.zh: 仁元母顧其婦及女曰：「禍將及矣，曷早計！」

translations.literal: Renyuan's mother turned to his wife and daughters and said: "Disaster is about to strike; why not plan early!"
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan's mother turned to his wife and daughters and said: "Disaster is about to strike—why not act now!"

sentences.zh: 皆死之。

translations.literal: They all died.
translations.idiomatic: They all took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 城陷，仁元父及弟並不屈死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Renyuan's father and younger brother also died rather than submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Renyuan's father and younger brother also died rather than submit.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔贈知府銜。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict posthumously granted him the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict posthumously granted him the honorary rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 與衍慶合祠於鄱陽，別於樂平建仁元專祠，父予墀、母陳氏、妻金氏、弟誠元、妹三人、妾楊氏及僕、婦等均附祀。

translations.literal: He was enshrined together with Yanqing at Poyang; a separate dedicated shrine to Renyuan was built at Leping, with his father Yu Chi, mother née Chen, wife née Jin, younger brother Chengyuan, three sisters, concubine née Yang, and servants and women of the household enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined together with Yanqing at Poyang, and a separate shrine to Renyuan was built at Leping. His father Yu Chi, mother née Chen, wife née Jin, younger brother Chengyuan, three sisters, concubine née Yang, and servants and women of the household were enshrined alongside him.

sentences.zh: 李福培，字仲謙，江蘇無錫人。

translations.literal: Li Fupei, style name Zhongqian, was a native of Wuxi County, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fupei, styled Zhongqian, was a native of Wuxi County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光二年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of the second year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren of the second year of Daoguang.

sentences.zh: 會試十三次不遇，考教習，補左翼宗學教習。

translations.literal: He failed the metropolitan examination thirteen times, passed the instructor examination, and was appointed instructor at the Left Wing Imperial Clan School.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the metropolitan examination thirteen times, he passed the instructor examination and was appointed instructor at the Left Wing Imperial Clan School.

sentences.zh: 期滿，用知縣，咸豐元年，選授廣東從化縣。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed district magistrate; in the first year of Xianfeng he was selected and appointed to Conghua County in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed district magistrate, and in the first year of Xianfeng was selected for Conghua County in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 時廣西賊起，廣州為賊出沒所，從化界連七邑，距府城百七十里。

translations.literal: At that time bandits had risen in Guangxi; Guangzhou was a haunt of bandit raids. Conghua bordered seven districts and lay one hundred seventy li from the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits had risen in Guangxi, and Guangzhou was a haunt of rebel raids. Conghua bordered seven districts and lay one hundred seventy li from the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊偪廣州，福培以花縣之石角及縣境之太平場為從化及諸邑屏障，請大府屯兵二千，兼可斷賊糧道，不報。

translations.literal: In the fourth year bandits pressed Guangzhou. Fupei argued that Shijiao in Huaxian County and Taiping Market within his jurisdiction were the shield for Conghua and neighboring districts, and requested that the provincial authorities station two thousand troops there to cut the bandits' grain route as well. No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year rebels pressed Guangzhou. Fupei argued that Shijiao in Huaxian and Taiping Market in his jurisdiction were the shield for Conghua and neighboring districts, and asked the provincial authorities to station two thousand troops there to cut the rebels' grain route as well. No reply came.

sentences.zh: 乃自募壯丁數百人，與典史趙應端及從弟性培分將之。

translations.literal: He therefore recruited several hundred able-bodied men himself and, together with the jail superintendent Zhao Yingduan and his younger cousin Xingpei, divided command among them.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore recruited several hundred able-bodied men himself and, with jail superintendent Zhao Yingduan and his younger cousin Xingpei, divided command among them.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊數千直薄城下，福培登陴固守，率兵民力戰，凡七捷，斬八百餘級。

translations.literal: In the seventh month several thousand bandits pressed straight to the walls. Fupei mounted the ramparts and held firm, leading soldiers and civilians in fierce fighting. They won seven victories in all and beheaded more than eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month several thousand rebels pressed straight to the walls. Fupei mounted the ramparts and held firm, leading soldiers and civilians in fierce fighting. They won seven victories in all and killed more than eight hundred.

sentences.zh: 九月，援賊大至，急解縣印授其子送省會，而誓以死守。

translations.literal: In the ninth month relieving bandits arrived in force. He urgently removed the county seal and gave it to his son to carry to the provincial capital, then swore to hold to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month relieving rebels arrived in force. He urgently removed the county seal and sent it with his son to the provincial capital, then swore to hold to the death.

sentences.zh: 賊舁砲攻城，裂數丈，賊蜂擁入。

translations.literal: The bandits brought up cannon to batter the wall, opening a breach several zhang wide, and swarmed in.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels brought up cannon, opened a breach several zhang wide, and swarmed in.

sentences.zh: 與應端、性培等巷戰，身受數傷，退至學宮尊經閣，猶投石殪賊，賊焚閣，三人同死之。

translations.literal: He fought in the lanes with Yingduan, Xingpei, and others, receiving several wounds. They retreated to the Zunjing Pavilion in the Confucian school, where he still hurled stones and killed bandits. The bandits burned the pavilion and all three died together.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the lanes with Yingduan, Xingpei, and others and took several wounds. They retreated to the Zunjing Pavilion in the Confucian school, where he still hurled stones and killed rebels. The rebels burned the pavilion and all three died together.

sentences.zh: 僕週鏞、勇丁蘇兆英等皆殉難。

translations.literal: His servant Zhou Yong and militiaman Su Zhaoying and others all died in the defense.
translations.idiomatic: His servant Zhou Yong, militiaman Su Zhaoying, and others all died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 卹福培贈知府銜，建專祠，特諡剛烈。

translations.literal: Fupei was posthumously granted the rank of prefect; a dedicated shrine was built, and he was specially granted the honorific Ganglie.
translations.idiomatic: Fupei was posthumously granted the honorary rank of prefect; a dedicated shrine was built, and he was specially granted the honorific title Ganglie, "Fierce Integrity."

sentences.zh: 福培就義處有血影漬地，如人形，濯之愈顯，後任建石欄護之，榜曰「忠跡昭然」。

translations.literal: Where Fupei met his death, a bloodstain soaked the ground in the shape of a human figure; the more it was washed, the clearer it became. A later official built a stone railing to protect it and posted a plaque reading "Loyal Deeds Clearly Manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Where Fupei met his death, a bloodstain soaked the ground in the shape of a human figure; the more it was washed, the clearer it became. A later official built a stone railing to protect it and posted a plaque reading "Loyal Deeds Clearly Manifest."

sentences.zh: 王恩綬，字樂山，亦無錫人。

translations.literal: Wang Enshou, style name Leshan, was also a native of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Enshou, styled Leshan, was also from Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 與福培為中表昆弟。

translations.literal: He and Fupei were cousins.
translations.idiomatic: He and Fupei were cousins.

sentences.zh: 少以諸生受知巡撫林則徐，招入節署讀書，稱為篤行君子。

translations.literal: As a young licentiate he won the favor of Governor Lin Zexu, who invited him to study in his yamen and called him a man of steadfast conduct.
translations.idiomatic: As a young licentiate he won the favor of Governor Lin Zexu, who invited him to study in his yamen and called him a man of steadfast conduct.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年順天鄉試舉人，考充宗學教習，勤其職。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of the Shuntian examination in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, he passed the examination and served as instructor at the Imperial Clan School, diligently performing his duties.
translations.idiomatic: A juren of the Shuntian examination in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, he passed the instructor examination and served at the Imperial Clan School, diligently performing his duties.

sentences.zh: 惠親王稽察宗學，語人曰：「不視此職為具文，孜孜不倦者，王教習一人而已。」

translations.literal: When Prince Hui inspected the Imperial Clan School, he told others: "Of those who do not treat this post as a mere formality and who work tirelessly, Instructor Wang alone is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hui inspected the Imperial Clan School, he said: "Of those who do not treat this post as a mere formality and who work tirelessly, Instructor Wang alone is such a man."

sentences.zh: 期滿，以知縣候選。

translations.literal: When his term expired he entered the pool of candidates for district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he entered the pool of candidates for district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 恩綬幼與福培同學，長以氣節相砥礪。

translations.literal: Enshou had studied with Fupei from youth; as adults they tempered each other's resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Enshou had studied with Fupei from youth; as adults they tempered each other's resolve and integrity.

sentences.zh: 同居京師，夜分論時事，慷慨罵諸將吏棄城與軍，輒面發赤。

translations.literal: Living together in the capital, they would discuss current affairs late into the night. Enshou would passionately denounce the generals and officials who abandoned cities and troops, his face flushing red each time.
translations.idiomatic: Living together in the capital, they discussed current affairs late into the night. Enshou would passionately denounce the generals and officials who abandoned cities and troops, his face flushing red each time.

sentences.zh: 戟手搏案，聲震鄰舍，僮僕為驚起。

translations.literal: He would brandish his hand and pound the table until the sound shook the neighboring houses and the servants were startled awake.
translations.idiomatic: He would brandish his hand and pound the table until the sound shook the neighboring houses and the servants were startled awake.

sentences.zh: 福培仕廣東，恩綬與之書曰：「大丈夫當此時，與其老死牖下，孰若埋骨疆場耶？」

translations.literal: When Fupei took office in Guangdong, Enshou wrote to him: "At a time like this, is it not better for a true man to leave his bones on the battlefield than to die old beneath his window?"
translations.idiomatic: When Fupei took office in Guangdong, Enshou wrote to him: "At a time like this, is it not better for a true man to leave his bones on the battlefield than to die old beneath his window?"

sentences.zh: 及福培殉，益躍躍欲得一當。

translations.literal: When Fupei died in the defense, Enshou grew all the more eager to seize his chance.
translations.idiomatic: When Fupei died in the defense, Enshou grew all the more eager to seize his chance.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，武漢克復，當事以恩綬死事狀上聞，得旨賜祭葬，予諡武愍。

translations.literal: The next winter Wuhan was recovered. The authorities reported Enshou's death in service to the throne; an edict granted sacrificial honors and burial rites and conferred the posthumous title Wumin.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Wuhan was recovered. The authorities reported Enshou's death in service to the throne; an edict granted sacrificial honors and burial rites and conferred the posthumous title Wumin, "Martyr of Martial Loyalty."

sentences.zh: 既而御史汪朝棨疏言：「恩綬無守土責，而視死如歸，不特與草間偷活判若天淵，即較之城亡與亡亦分難易。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Censor Wang Chaoqi memorialized: "Enshou had no duty to defend territory, yet he faced death as if returning home. This is not merely as far from skulking alive in the grass as heaven from the abyss; even compared with dying when one's city falls, the difficulty differs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Censor Wang Chaoqi memorialized: "Enshou had no duty to defend territory, yet he faced death as if returning home. This is not merely as far from skulking alive in the grass as heaven from the abyss; even compared with dying when one's city falls, the difficulty differs.

sentences.zh: 且忠孝一門，僕從皆知赴戰，尤足扶植綱常。

translations.literal: Moreover, loyalty and filial piety were united in one household, and even servants knew to go into battle—this is especially fit to uphold the moral order.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, loyalty and filial piety were united in one household, and even servants knew to go into battle—this is especially fit to uphold the moral order.

sentences.zh: 請於本籍建專祠。」

translations.literal: I request that a dedicated shrine be built in his native place."
translations.idiomatic: I request that a dedicated shrine be built in his native place."

sentences.zh: 會巡撫郭柏廕亦疏請建祠武昌，詔並許之。

translations.literal: At the same time Governor Guo Baoyin also memorialized asking for a shrine at Wuchang; an edict granted both requests.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Governor Guo Baoyin also memorialized asking for a shrine at Wuchang; an edict granted both requests.

sentences.zh: 李右文，字伯蘭，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Li Youwen, style name Bolan, was a native of Tongzhou, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Youwen, styled Bolan, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 舉人，

translations.literal: A provincial graduate,
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren.

sentences.zh: 選授湖南東安知縣。

translations.literal: he was selected and appointed magistrate of Dong'an in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected and appointed magistrate of Dong'an in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 粵匪犯天津，留辦本籍團練，以功賞知州銜。

translations.literal: When Guangdong bandits threatened Tianjin, he remained to organize local militia in his native place and was awarded the rank of prefect for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels threatened Tianjin, he remained to organize local militia in his native place and was awarded the honorary rank of prefect for his merit.

sentences.zh: 五年，赴官，值湘南道梗，諸弟馳書尼其行，不聽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he set out to take office. The roads in southern Hunan were blocked; his younger brothers sent urgent letters trying to stop him, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he set out to take office. The roads in southern Hunan were blocked; his younger brothers sent urgent letters trying to stop him, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至楚，權新寧。

translations.literal: When he reached Chu he served as acting magistrate of Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Hunan he served as acting magistrate of Xinning.

sentences.zh: 邑屢被寇，戶口流亡，右文招集撫循，凋敝以振。

translations.literal: The district had repeatedly suffered raids; the population had fled. Youwen gathered and comforted them, reviving the wasted land.
translations.idiomatic: The district had repeatedly suffered raids and the population had fled. Youwen gathered and comforted the people, reviving the wasted land.

sentences.zh: 七年，以最調祁陽，時從弟載文殉難廣西，弟复馳書勸歸，慨然曰：「死生命也，脫捐頂踵報國，是得死所也，何慮為！」

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Qiyang for outstanding service. At that time his cousin Zaiwen had died in Guangxi; his brothers again sent urgent letters urging him to return. He said with feeling: "Life and death are fate. If I can give even my head and heels to serve the state, that is finding the right place to die—what is there to worry about!"
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to Qiyang for outstanding service. His cousin Zaiwen had just died in Guangxi, and his brothers again sent urgent letters urging him to return. He said with feeling: "Life and death are fate. If I can give even my head and heels to serve the state, that is finding the right place to die—what is there to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 尋回東安任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned to his post at Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he returned to his post at Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 八年，湖南境賊退，右文謂眾曰：「賊敗他竄，不可恃。」

translations.literal: In the eighth year the bandits withdrew from Hunan. Youwen told the people: "The bandits have been defeated and fled elsewhere; we cannot rely on that."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the rebels withdrew from Hunan. Youwen told the people: "The rebels have been beaten and fled elsewhere—we cannot rely on that."

sentences.zh: 亟訓練民團，置倉穀數千石，備不虞。

translations.literal: He urgently trained the local militia and stored several thousand shi of grain as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently trained the local militia and stored several thousand shi of grain against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 九年春，石達開由江西回竄湖南，逼近東安，新寧紳眾數百人來迎，請避賊新寧。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year Shi Dakai fled back from Jiangxi into Hunan and approached Dong'an. Several hundred gentry from Xinning came to welcome him and asked him to flee the bandits to Xinning.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Shi Dakai fled back from Jiangxi into Hunan and approached Dong'an. Several hundred gentry from Xinning came to welcome him and asked him to flee the rebels to Xinning.

sentences.zh: 右文曰：「吾去，誰為守此土者？」

translations.literal: Youwen said: "If I leave, who will defend this land?"
translations.idiomatic: Youwen said: "If I leave, who will defend this land?"

sentences.zh: 已，復請護家口出境，又曰：「是為民望也。」

translations.literal: Then they again asked that his family be escorted out of the district. He said again: "That would destroy the people's hope."
translations.idiomatic: Then they again asked that his family be escorted out of the district. He said again: "That would destroy the people's hope."

sentences.zh: 卻其請。

translations.literal: He refused their request.
translations.idiomatic: He refused their request.

sentences.zh: 眾泣，誓死不忍去。

translations.literal: The people wept and swore they could not bear to leave and would die if need be.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept and swore they could not bear to leave and would die if need be.

sentences.zh: 三月，賊麕至，城卑，四面皆山，賊環瞰之。

translations.literal: In the third month the bandits gathered and arrived. The walls were low; mountains surrounded the city on every side, and the bandits looked down on it from all around.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the rebels gathered and arrived. The walls were low; mountains surrounded the city on every side, and the rebels looked down on it from all around.

sentences.zh: 右文集城中官民登陴固守，親冒矢石，曆七晝夜，轟斃城下賊甚夥。

translations.literal: Youwen gathered officials and civilians in the city to mount the ramparts and hold firm. He personally braved arrows and stones. For seven days and nights cannon fire killed many bandits below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Youwen gathered officials and civilians to mount the ramparts and hold firm. He personally braved arrows and stones. For seven days and nights cannon fire killed many rebels below the walls.

sentences.zh: 城陷，與賊巷戰署東，身被重創，猶手刃數賊，力竭遇害，賊燔其屍，僅得脊骨歸葬。

translations.literal: When the city fell he fought the bandits in the lanes east of the yamen. He received grave wounds but still killed several bandits with his own hand. When his strength was spent he was killed. The bandits burned his body; only his spine was recovered for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he fought the rebels in the lanes east of the yamen. He was gravely wounded but still cut down several with his own hand. When his strength gave out he was killed. The rebels burned his body; only his spine was recovered for burial.

sentences.zh: 子傑、妻郝、子婦王，及僕婢，皆從死。

translations.literal: His son Jie, wife née Hao, daughter-in-law née Wang, and servants and maids all died with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jie, wife née Hao, daughter-in-law née Wang, and servants and maids all died with him.

sentences.zh: 新寧紳眾數百，亦先後戰死。

translations.literal: Several hundred gentry from Xinning also died in battle one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred gentry from Xinning also fell in battle one after another.

sentences.zh: 詔視道員例賜卹，建祠本籍，隨殉親丁、紳勇附祀。

translations.literal: An edict granted posthumous honors according to the regulations for a circuit intendant, ordered a shrine built in his native place, and enshrined alongside him the kin, gentry, and militia who died with him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted posthumous honors according to the regulations for a circuit intendant, ordered a shrine built in his native place, and enshrined alongside him the kin, gentry, and militia who died with him.

sentences.zh: 子傑，字小蘭。

translations.literal: Jie, style name Xiaolan.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, styled Xiaolan.

sentences.zh: 縣丞。

translations.literal: Assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He was an assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 有幹略，侍父湖南，襄督練勇，進知縣。

translations.literal: Capable and resourceful, he attended his father in Hunan, assisted in organizing the militia, and was promoted to district magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Capable and resourceful, he attended his father in Hunan, helped organize the militia, and was promoted to district magistrate.

sentences.zh: 方賊之回竄也，右文知不免，作書與諸弟訣，命傑齎往，意欲生之也。

translations.literal: When the bandits were fleeing back, Youwen knew he could not escape. He wrote farewell letters to his younger brothers and ordered Jie to carry them, intending to keep him alive.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were fleeing back, Youwen knew he could not escape. He wrote farewell letters to his younger brothers and ordered Jie to carry them, intending to keep him alive.

sentences.zh: 傑不忍去，又重逆父命，潛避署左右，觀賊變。

translations.literal: Jie could not bear to leave, yet he also could not lightly disobey his father's command. He hid secretly near the yamen to watch how the bandits would act.
translations.idiomatic: Jie could not bear to leave, yet he also could not lightly disobey his father's command. He hid secretly near the yamen to watch how the rebels would act.

sentences.zh: 賊至，率練勇守南門，城陷，聞警馳父所，未至，遇害，屍同被焚。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived he led the militia to defend the south gate. When the city fell he heard the alarm and raced to his father's side. Before he arrived he was killed; his body was burned as well.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived he led the militia to defend the south gate. When the city fell he heard the alarm and raced to his father's side. Before he arrived he was killed; his body was burned as well.

sentences.zh: 視同知例賜卹。

translations.literal: Posthumous honors were granted according to the regulations for a subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous honors were granted according to the regulations for a subprefect.

sentences.zh: 載文，字潞帆，右文從弟。

translations.literal: Zaiwen, style name Lufan, was Youwen's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiwen, styled Lufan, was Youwen's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a juren.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以知縣發廣西，咸豐元年，權馬平縣。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was dispatched to Guangxi as district magistrate; in the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Maping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was sent to Guangxi as district magistrate; in the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Maping County.

sentences.zh: 時洪秀全犯桂林，馬平賊李志信響應，載文率兵剿捕，殲之。

translations.literal: At that time Hong Xiuquan attacked Guilin; the Maping bandit Li Zhixin responded. Zaiwen led troops to suppress and capture them, exterminating the band.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong Xiuquan attacked Guilin, the Maping bandit Li Zhixin rose in response. Zaiwen led troops to suppress them and wiped out the band.

sentences.zh: 尋調平南，五年，艇匪梁培友由梧州上竄，陷潯州，擾平南，載文御之渡口，砲轟沉其船，追擊斃匪無數。

translations.literal: He was soon transferred to Pingnan. In the fifth year the boat bandit Liang Peiyou fled upriver from Wuzhou, captured Xunzhou, and harassed Pingnan. Zaiwen met him at the ferry crossing; cannon fire sank his boats, and in pursuit countless bandits were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Pingnan. In the fifth year the boat bandit Liang Peiyou fled upriver from Wuzhou, took Xunzhou, and harassed Pingnan. Zaiwen met him at the ferry crossing; cannon fire sank his boats, and in pursuit countless rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 賊屢分撲南北岸，悉卻之。

translations.literal: The bandits repeatedly split forces to strike the north and south banks; he drove them all back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels repeatedly split forces to strike the north and south banks; he drove them all back.

sentences.zh: 累以功擢同知直隸州。

translations.literal: For repeated merit he was promoted to subprefect of a directly administered prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For repeated merit he was promoted to subprefect of a directly administered prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年五月至七月，賊麕至，水陸環攻，載文偕參將曾廷相、張遇清，都司唐文燦等，嬰城固守，困重圍七十餘日。

translations.literal: From the fifth to the seventh month of the sixth year bandits arrived in swarms; by land and water they encircled and attacked. Zaiwen together with regimental commanders Zeng Tingxiang and Zhang Yuqing, battalion commander Tang Wencan, and others held the city firm under siege, trapped in heavy encirclement for more than seventy days.
translations.idiomatic: From May through July of the sixth year rebels swarmed in; by land and water they encircled the city and assaulted it. Zaiwen, together with regimental commanders Zeng Tingxiang and Zhang Yuqing, battalion commander Tang Wencan, and others, held firm behind the walls, trapped under heavy siege for more than seventy days.

sentences.zh: 乞援、乞餉，告急文數十上，大吏但空言慰藉。

translations.literal: They begged for reinforcements and supplies; urgent dispatches went up dozens of times, but the high officials offered only empty words of consolation.
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded for reinforcements and supplies and sent dozens of urgent appeals, but the senior officials offered only empty words of comfort.

sentences.zh: 載文知事不可為，遣親僕間道以縣印檄送桂林，獨激勵兵勇與賊相持，教諭傅揚清，把總呂耀文，生員傅揚芬、吳國霖先後戰死。

translations.literal: Zaiwen knew the situation could not be saved. He sent a trusted servant by a secret route to carry the county seal and dispatch to Guilin. He alone roused the troops and militia to hold out against the bandits. The instructor Fu Yangqing, platoon commander Lü Yaowen, and students Fu Yangfen and Wu Guolin died in battle one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the situation was hopeless, Zaiwen sent a trusted servant by a secret route to Guilin with the county seal and official dispatches. He alone rallied the troops and militia to hold out against the rebels. The instructor Fu Yangqing, platoon commander Lü Yaowen, and students Fu Yangfen and Wu Guolin fell in battle one after another.

sentences.zh: 賊攻益急，載文中砲傷腿，痛哭，北面頓首曰：「臣力盡，惟以一死報國，然不忍百姓屠戮也。」

translations.literal: The bandits pressed their attack ever harder. Zaiwen was wounded in the leg by cannon fire. Weeping, he bowed his head to the north and said: "My strength is spent; I can only repay the state with my death, yet I cannot bear to see the people slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: As the rebel assault grew fiercer, Zaiwen was struck in the leg by cannon fire. In tears he bowed toward the north and said: "My strength is spent; I can repay the state only with my life, yet I cannot bear to see the people massacred."

sentences.zh: 縱之去。

translations.literal: He let them go.
translations.idiomatic: He let the people leave.

sentences.zh: 千總方源開城私遁，賊乘隙入。

translations.literal: Company commander Fang Yuan opened the gate and fled in secret; the bandits seized the opening and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Company commander Fang Yuan opened the gates and slipped away in secret, and the rebels poured through the breach.

sentences.zh: 載文、廷相率勇巷戰，手刃數十賊，力竭，自剄不殊，賊擁至船中，抗罵不屈，並臠割之。

translations.literal: Zaiwen and Tingxiang led the militia in street fighting and personally killed dozens of bandits. Strength exhausted, Zaiwen cut his own throat but did not die immediately. The bandits hauled him to a boat; he resisted and cursed without yielding, and they cut him to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiwen and Tingxiang led the militia in street fighting and personally killed dozens of rebels. When their strength was spent Zaiwen slit his own throat but did not die at once. The rebels dragged him onto a boat; he resisted and cursed without yielding, and they hacked him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 是役也，遇清守北門，持大刀斫賊三十餘，被賊攢刺無完膚，死。

translations.literal: In this battle Yuqing defended the north gate, wielding a great sword and hacking down more than thirty bandits. The bandits stabbed him from all sides until no patch of skin was whole, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Yuqing held the north gate, wielding a great sword and cutting down more than thirty rebels. They stabbed him from every side until not an inch of skin was whole, and he died.

sentences.zh: 文燦守南城，率外委張珽巷戰死。

translations.literal: Wencan defended the south wall and led the junior clerk Zhang Ting in street fighting to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Wencan held the south wall and led the junior clerk Zhang Ting in street fighting until both were killed.

sentences.zh: 守備張彪守火藥局，燃火轟斃賊百餘，亦戰死。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Zhang Biao guarded the powder magazine, set fire and blasted more than a hundred bandits to death, and also died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Zhang Biao guarded the powder magazine, detonated it, and blew more than a hundred rebels to death; he too died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 載文、廷相死尤慘。

translations.literal: The deaths of Zaiwen and Tingxiang were especially horrific.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiwen and Tingxiang died especially horrific deaths.

sentences.zh: 先是巡撫勞崇光奏薦載文堪勝道府，兵部侍郎王茂廕亦奏保循聲卓著，擢桂林遺缺知府。

translations.literal: Earlier the governor Luo Chongguang had memorialized recommending Zaiwen as fit to hold a circuit or prefectural post. Vice Minister of War Wang Maoyin also memorialized commending his outstanding reputation for upright conduct. He was promoted to fill the vacant post of prefect of Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Governor Luo Chongguang had recommended Zaiwen as capable of serving at circuit or prefectural level. Vice Minister of War Wang Maoyin had also commended his outstanding reputation for upright governance. He was promoted to fill the vacant post of prefect of Guilin.

sentences.zh: 命下，載文已遇害。

translations.literal: When the order arrived, Zaiwen had already been killed.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the appointment reached him, Zaiwen had already been killed.

sentences.zh: 贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職，建祠本籍。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and awarded hereditary rank; a shrine was built in his native place.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the honorary rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and awarded hereditary honors; a shrine was erected in his native place.

sentences.zh: 同治十年，追諡壯烈。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he was posthumously granted the honorific Zhuanglie.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Tongzhi he was posthumously granted the honorific title Zhuanglie, "Heroic Martyrdom."

sentences.zh: 李榞，字紫籓，安徽宣城人。

translations.literal: Li Yuan, style name Zifan, was a native of Xuancheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan, styled Zifan, was a native of Xuancheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 以監生入貲為知縣，，選授湖北公安，賑災有惠政。

translations.literal: As a student of the Imperial Academy he purchased appointment as district magistrate and was selected and assigned to Gong'an in Hubei, where disaster relief brought benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: As an Imperial Academy student he purchased appointment as district magistrate and was assigned to Gong'an in Hubei, where his disaster relief earned him a reputation for benevolent governance.

sentences.zh: 調孝感，再調鍾祥。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Xiaogan, then again to Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Xiaogan and then to Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪自長沙躪岳州，犯武昌，所在奸民競起，鍾祥馬騾子、襄陽郭大安、天門蓋天王皆盜魁，黨眾大者萬餘，小乃數千。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng Cantonese bandits swept from Changsha through Yuezhou and attacked Wuchang; local villains rose up everywhere. Zhongxiang's Ma Luozi, Xiangyang's Guo Da'an, and Tianmen's Gai Tianwang were all bandit chiefs, their followers numbering as many as ten thousand or more at the largest and several thousand at the smallest.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng Cantonese rebels swept from Changsha through Yuezhou and struck at Wuchang, and local villains rose up everywhere. Ma Luozi of Zhongxiang, Guo Da'an of Xiangyang, and Gai Tianwang of Tianmen were all bandit chiefs, with followings numbering from several thousand up to more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 榞教練壯士千餘人，捕馬騾子及其黨數十人斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan trained more than a thousand stalwart men, captured Ma Luozi and dozens of his followers, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan trained more than a thousand stalwart men, captured Ma Luozi and dozens of his followers, and had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 偵知郭大安方謀以眾投粵賊，設伏間道擒之。

translations.literal: Learning that Guo Da'an was plotting to lead his followers to join the Cantonese bandits, he laid an ambush on a side route and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Guo Da'an was plotting to bring his followers over to the Cantonese rebels, he set an ambush on a side route and captured him.

sentences.zh: 乘大霧掩擊蓋天王，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: Taking advantage of heavy fog he launched a surprise attack on Gai Tianwang and captured all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Exploiting a heavy fog he struck Gai Tianwang by surprise and captured his entire band.

sentences.zh: 時武昌、漢陽相繼陷，上游諸郡帖然無恐者，榞平諸盜力也。

translations.literal: At that time Wuchang and Hanyang fell in succession; of the upstream prefectures only those Yuan had pacified remained calm without fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang and Hanyang fell in succession, the upstream prefectures remained calm and unafraid only where Yuan had suppressed the bandits.

sentences.zh: 既而武昌复，大吏上榞功，擢荊門州知州，調署江夏縣，鍾祥民萬眾攀留不得。

translations.literal: Later Wuchang was recovered; the high officials reported Yuan's merit, and he was promoted to magistrate of Jingmen Prefecture and transferred to serve as acting magistrate of Jiangxia County. Tens of thousands of people in Zhongxiang clung to him and begged him to stay, but could not keep him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang was recovered the senior officials reported Yuan's merits. He was promoted to magistrate of Jingmen Prefecture and transferred to serve as acting magistrate of Jiangxia County. Tens of thousands of people in Zhongxiang clung to him and pleaded for him to stay, but in vain.

sentences.zh: 會粵匪林鳳祥等北犯，其後隊自河南折入湖北，陷黃梅，趨麻城。

translations.literal: At that time the Cantonese bandits Lin Fengxiang and others invaded north; their rear column turned in from Henan into Hubei, captured Huangmei, and pressed toward Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Cantonese rebels Lin Fengxiang and others pushed north; their rear column turned from Henan into Hubei, took Huangmei, and pressed toward Macheng.

sentences.zh: 榞率提標兵千人往援，擊賊黃岡之鵝公頸江口，大破之，窮追至安慶，與安慶兵夾擊，殲賊殆盡。

translations.literal: Yuan led a thousand provincial banner troops to reinforce them. He attacked the bandits at Egojing on the Yangtze in Huanggang and routed them, pursued them to Anqing, and in concert with the Anqing troops destroyed the bandits nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan led a thousand provincial banner troops to their aid, routed the rebels at Egojing on the Yangtze in Huanggang, pursued them all the way to Anqing, and together with the Anqing garrison nearly wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 還值宿松警，复破賊下倉埠，詔以知府升用。

translations.literal: On his return he met the alarm at Susong and again defeated the bandits at Xiacangbu. An edict ordered his promotion for use as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he met an alarm at Susong and again defeated the rebels at Xiacangbu. An edict ordered him promoted for appointment as prefect.

sentences.zh: 踰月，賊復自江西大至，寇廣濟之田家鎮，大吏檄榞往，連戰皆捷。
