translations.literal: Within a month the bandits again came in force from Jiangxi and raided Tianjiazhen in Guangji. The high officials dispatched Yuan there, and in battle after battle he was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the rebels again poured in from Jiangxi and raided Tianjiazhen in Guangji. The senior officials ordered Yuan there, and he won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 最後戰，他將懦不進，榞率所部渡江擊賊。

translations.literal: In the final battle other generals were too timid to advance. Yuan led his own troops across the river to attack the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the final battle the other commanders hung back in fear. Yuan led his own troops across the river to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊敗走，孤軍追賊，至興國州富池口，賊知榞軍無繼者，分舟中賊登岸襲其後。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated and fled. With a lone force he pursued them to Fuchikou in Xingguo Prefecture. The bandits knew Yuan's army had no reinforcements; bandits from the boats went ashore and struck from the rear.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were routed and fled. Yuan pursued them alone as far as Fuchikou in Xingguo Prefecture. Seeing that his force had no backup, the rebels sent men from their boats ashore to strike from the rear.

sentences.zh: 榞引就水軍，水軍走左，陷淖中，與所部二百人皆鬥死，咸豐三年九月十日也。

translations.literal: Yuan turned toward the naval forces, but the sailors fled to the left and sank into the mire. He and his two hundred men all died fighting. It was the tenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Xianfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan turned toward the naval forces, but the sailors broke left and foundered in the mud. He and his two hundred men all died fighting. It was the tenth day of the ninth month of the third year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈道銜，予世職。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was posthumously granted the rank of circuit intendant and awarded hereditary rank.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne he was posthumously granted the honorary rank of circuit intendant and awarded hereditary honors.

sentences.zh: 公安、鍾祥之民，家祭巷哭，奉木主祀之。

translations.literal: The people of Gong'an and Zhongxiang offered household sacrifices and wept in the lanes, enshrining wooden tablets to worship him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Gong'an and Zhongxiang held household sacrifices and wept in the streets, enshrining spirit tablets in his honor.

sentences.zh: 始榞為縣，所至必於其地夷險豐耗、民俗醇訛、姦蠹根株、人所疾苦盡知之。

translations.literal: From the time Yuan served as magistrate, wherever he went he thoroughly understood that place's terrain and its hardship or ease, its abundance or scarcity, whether custom was upright or corrupt, the roots of malfeasance and corruption, and the people's sufferings.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Yuan served as magistrate, wherever he went he made it his business to know the terrain—where it was harsh or easy, where there was want or plenty—whether local custom was upright or corrupt, where corruption had taken root, and what the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 為治行之出於至誠，人樂為用，原效死力。

translations.literal: Because his conduct in governing sprang from utmost sincerity, people were glad to serve him and were willing to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Because his governance sprang from utter sincerity, people were glad to serve him and willing to die in his cause.

sentences.zh: 及其殉難，久而思之。

translations.literal: After he died in loyal service, they remembered him long afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Long after he gave his life in service, they still remembered him.

sentences.zh: 同治二年，湖北大吏復奏榞死事甚烈，在官政績尤著，請宣城及死事所建專祠，詔可，予諡剛介。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi the high officials of Hubei again memorialized that Yuan's death in service was exceedingly fierce and his official achievements especially outstanding, requesting dedicated shrines at Xuancheng and where he died. The throne approved and granted the posthumous honorific Gangjie.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi the senior officials of Hubei memorialized again that Yuan had died a fiercely loyal death and that his official achievements were especially distinguished, requesting dedicated shrines at Xuancheng and at the place where he fell. The throne approved and granted the posthumous title Gangjie, "Firm Integrity."

sentences.zh: 陳肖儀，字幼泉，江西弋陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Xiaoyi, style name Youquan, was a native of Yiyang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiaoyi, styled Youquan, was a native of Yiyang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 嘗遭母喪，扶柩舟行江中。

translations.literal: Once when his mother died he carried her coffin by boat on the river.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he traveled the river by boat bearing her coffin.

sentences.zh: 夜火發，四面皆烈焰，肖儀以身伏柩上，隨江流飄蕩，不死，柩亦無恙，一時稱奇孝。

translations.literal: At night fire broke out; flames blazed on every side. Xiaoyi lay his body atop the coffin and drifted with the current. He did not die, nor was the coffin harmed. For a time he was hailed for extraordinary filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: One night fire broke out and flames blazed on every side. Xiaoyi lay his body over the coffin and drifted with the current. He survived, and the coffin was unharmed. For a time he was hailed for extraordinary filial piety.

sentences.zh: 年十九，官湖北縣丞，擢廣濟知縣。

translations.literal: At nineteen he served as assistant magistrate in Hubei and was promoted to magistrate of Guangji.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he served as assistant magistrate in Hubei and was promoted to magistrate of Guangji.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪破田家鎮，去縣七十里，縣故無城垣，召募鄉兵，皆望風走。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Cantonese bandits broke Tianjiazhen, seventy li from the county seat. The county had no city walls. He summoned local militia, but all fled at the sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng Cantonese rebels overran Tianjiazhen, seventy li from the county seat. The county had no walls. He called up local militia, but they all fled at the first sign of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 肖儀知事不可為，持刃坐堂皇，賊入，數其罪，即抽刃自剄，未殊。

translations.literal: Xiaoyi knew nothing could be done. He sat in the main hall with a blade in hand. When the bandits entered he denounced their crimes, then drew the blade and cut his own throat, but did not die immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Realizing that all was lost, Xiaoyi sat in the main hall with a blade in hand. When the rebels entered he denounced their crimes, then drew the blade and cut his own throat, but did not die at once.

sentences.zh: 賊縛之，曳於市。

translations.literal: The bandits bound him and dragged him through the market.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound him and dragged him through the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 子恩藻奮臂擊賊，賊立殺之，肖儀罵益烈。

translations.literal: His son Enzao struck out at the bandits with flung arms. The bandits killed him at once, and Xiaoyi cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: His son Enzao lunged at the rebels, and they killed him on the spot. Xiaoyi cursed all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊鑿齒刳頰，膚盡見骨，三日乃死，賊解其體為五。

translations.literal: The bandits chiseled out his teeth and gouged his cheeks until flesh was gone and bone showed. After three days he died. The bandits cut his body into five parts.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels chiseled out his teeth and gouged his cheeks until flesh was stripped to the bone. After three days he died, and the rebels cut his body into five pieces.

sentences.zh: 縣民悲憤，賊去始斂焉。

translations.literal: The county people grieved and raged. Only after the bandits left did they gather his remains for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The county people grieved and raged. Only after the rebels withdrew did they gather his remains for burial.

sentences.zh: 萬成，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Wan Cheng was a man of the Bordered White Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Cheng was a Manchu of the Bordered White Banner.

sentences.zh: 道光二十四年舉人，揀發湖北知縣，署漢川，調安陸。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, he was selected for appointment as district magistrate in Hubei and served as acting magistrate of Hanchuan before transfer to Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: A juren in the twenty-fourth year of Daoguang, he was selected for appointment as district magistrate in Hubei, served as acting magistrate of Hanchuan, and was transferred to Anlu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，匪由武昌北竄，陷雲夢。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng bandits fled north from Wuchang and captured Yunmeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng rebels fled north from Wuchang and took Yunmeng.

sentences.zh: 時總督台湧駐兵德安，萬成陳戰守二策，湧不能用，欲退守三關，徐圖克復，且諷與俱去。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Tai Yong was encamped at De'an. Wan Cheng presented strategies for fighting and for holding firm. Yong could not use them and wished to fall back and hold the Three Passes, gradually planning recovery, and he hinted that Wan Cheng should leave with him.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Tai Yong was then encamped at De'an. Wan Cheng laid out plans for fighting and for holding the city, but Yong would not heed them. He wanted to fall back to the Three Passes and recover the territory gradually, and he hinted that Wan Cheng should leave with him.

sentences.zh: 萬成垂涕曰：「棄而不守，如百姓何​​？

translations.literal: Wan Cheng wept and said: "If we abandon the city and do not hold it, what will become of the people?
translations.idiomatic: Wan Cheng wept and said: "If we abandon the city and refuse to hold it, what will become of the people?

sentences.zh: 與城存亡，守土之義也！」

translations.literal: Sharing life and death with the city is the duty of one who holds the land!"
translations.idiomatic: To live or die with the city is the duty of one who holds the soil!"

sentences.zh: 其僕复勸之，並以主人無嗣為辭，萬成厲聲曰：「我家世受國恩，若臨難偷生，無以對國家，即無以對祖、父！」

translations.literal: His servant again urged him, pleading as well that his master had no heir. Wan Cheng said in a stern voice: "My family has received the state's grace for generations. If at a crisis I steal my life, I cannot face the state—nor can I face my ancestors and my father!"
translations.idiomatic: His servant urged him again, also pleading that his master had no heir. Wan Cheng said sternly: "My family has received the state's grace for generations. If at a crisis I steal my life, I cannot face the state—nor my ancestors and my father!"

sentences.zh: 遂致書邑紳曰：「禍在旦夕，誰之責歟？

translations.literal: He then wrote to the local gentry: "Disaster is imminent. Who bears the blame?
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote to the local gentry: "Disaster hangs by a thread. Who bears the blame?

sentences.zh: 一死塞責，不可為臣；

translations.literal: One death can discharge my duty; I cannot be a subject otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: One death can answer for my duty; otherwise I cannot be a loyal subject;

sentences.zh: 有辱於親，不可為子。

translations.literal: To bring shame upon my kin is to be no son.
translations.idiomatic: to bring shame on my kin is to be no son at all.

sentences.zh: 原不歸櫬於先人之墓，留葬於此，以志吾恨。」

translations.literal: I wish my coffin not to return to my forebears' tombs but to be buried here to record my grievance."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my coffin not return to my forebears' tombs, but be buried here to mark my grief."

sentences.zh: 是夜警報沓至，萬成召團練諸紳，告以在城兵勇俱隨總督北發，己當以死守城。

translations.literal: That night alarms came in one after another. Wan Cheng summoned the militia gentry and told them that all troops in the city had departed north with the governor-general and that he himself would hold the city to the death.
translations.idiomatic: That night alarm after alarm arrived. Wan Cheng summoned the militia gentry and told them that all troops in the city had marched north with the governor-general and that he would hold the city to the death.

sentences.zh: 又知事必不濟，復作絕命書，與士民訣，略曰：「賊已至雲夢，勢必來德安，我惟攖城固守。

translations.literal: Knowing the affair could not succeed, he also wrote a farewell letter to take leave of the gentry and people, saying in substance: "The bandits have reached Yunmeng and are sure to come to De'an. I can only hold the city firm under siege.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that all must fail, he also wrote a final letter to bid farewell to gentry and people, saying in essence: "The rebels have reached Yunmeng and will surely come to De'an. I can only hold the city under siege.

sentences.zh: 不能，則以死繼之。

translations.literal: If I cannot, I will follow with my death.
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot hold it, I will follow with my life.

sentences.zh: 諸君不我遐棄，能尋我遺骸，葬於碧霞台下，常此北望神京，則九原之下，感不忘矣！」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen do not abandon me from afar, if you can seek out my remains and bury them beneath Bixia Terrace, forever gazing north toward the sacred capital, then beneath the ninefold earth I shall be grateful beyond forgetting!"
translations.idiomatic: If you do not abandon me from afar, if you can find my remains and bury them beneath Bixia Terrace, ever facing north toward the capital, then in the land beyond I shall never forget your kindness!"

sentences.zh: 逾日，賊距城二十餘裡，台湧擁兵徑去。

translations.literal: The next day the bandits were twenty-odd li from the city, and Tai Yong marched off with his troops straight away.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the rebels were still more than twenty li from the city when Tai Yong marched away with his troops.

sentences.zh: 萬成謁知府議救急策，甫出署，紅巾賊數十突至。

translations.literal: Wan Cheng called on the prefect to discuss emergency measures. Just as he left the yamen, dozens of red-turbaned bandits burst in.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Cheng called on the prefect to discuss emergency measures. Just as he stepped out of the yamen, dozens of red-turbaned rebels burst upon him.

sentences.zh: 知城陷，抽佩刀與戰，手刃數人，力竭死之，賊焚裂其屍。

translations.literal: Learning the city had fallen, he drew his belt dagger and fought, personally killing several men. Strength exhausted, he died; the bandits burned and tore apart his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the city had fallen, he drew his belt dagger and fought, killing several men himself. When his strength gave out he died, and the rebels burned and mutilated his body.

sentences.zh: 德安复，縣民卒收葬殘骨於碧霞台下，以遂其志。

translations.literal: When De'an was recovered the county people at last gathered his scattered bones and buried them beneath Bixia Terrace, fulfilling his wish.
translations.idiomatic: When De'an was recovered the townspeople at last gathered his scattered bones and buried them beneath Bixia Terrace, fulfilling his wish.

sentences.zh: 袁祖德，字又村，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Yuan Zude, style name Youcun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zude, styled Youcun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 祖枚，以詩文名，官江寧，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mei was famed for poetry and prose, served in Jiangning, and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mei was famed for poetry and prose, held office in Jiangning, and settled the family there.

sentences.zh: 祖德早慧，入貲為江蘇寶山縣丞。

translations.literal: Zude showed precocious talent. He purchased appointment as assistant magistrate of Baoshan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zude was precocious. He purchased appointment as assistant magistrate of Baoshan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 兵備道某稔其才，以上海縣令姚某漕事詿誤去，檄祖德擢縣事，且代姚辦漕，未五月，難作。

translations.literal: A defense circuit intendant recognized his talent. When the magistrate of Shanghai surnamed Yao was dismissed for errors in the grain-transport service, he ordered Zude promoted to the county post and also to handle the transport in Yao's place. Within five months disaster broke out.
translations.idiomatic: A circuit intendant for defense recognized his talent. When the magistrate of Shanghai, surnamed Yao, was dismissed over errors in the grain-transport service, he ordered Zude promoted to the county post and to take over the transport duties as well. Within five months crisis erupted.

sentences.zh: 先是縣中團練多閩、廣無賴，本地遊民和之，漫無紀律。

translations.literal: Earlier the county militia had largely been ruffians from Fujian and Guangdong; local drifters joined them, and discipline was altogether lacking.
translations.idiomatic: The county militia had largely been ruffians from Fujian and Guangdong, with local drifters falling in alongside them and no discipline at all.

sentences.zh: 粵匪據江寧為偽都，人心益搖，於是小刀會起事。

translations.literal: Cantonese bandits held Jiangning as their false capital, hearts wavered all the more, and then the Small Sword Society rose in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels held Jiangning as their false capital, morale wavered ever more, and then the Small Sword Society rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 小刀會者，即無賴遊民所結合，黨羽散佈，官役皆為耳目。

translations.literal: The Small Sword Society was a combination of idle ruffians and drifters; its partisans were scattered everywhere, and yamen runners served as its eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: The Small Sword Society was an alliance of idle ruffians and drifters; its members were scattered everywhere, and yamen clerks and runners served as its eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 道故粵產，謂中多粵人，置不為備；

translations.literal: The intendant was himself a native of Guangdong and, thinking many among them were Cantonese, made no preparations;
translations.idiomatic: The intendant was himself a Cantonese native and, assuming many members were fellow Cantonese, took no precautions;

sentences.zh: 先發難嘉定，戕縣官，道仍不為備。

translations.literal: they first rose in Jiading and killed the county magistrate, yet the intendant still made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: they first rose in Jiading and killed the county magistrate, yet he still made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年八月初五日為上丁祀事日，黎明，祖德肅衣冠出，賊蟻擁入署。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the eighth month of the third year of Xianfeng, the upper day of sacrifice, at dawn Zude came out in full formal dress. Bandits swarmed into the yamen like ants.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the eighth month of the third year of Xianfeng—the upper day of sacrifice—Zude came out at dawn in full formal dress. Rebels swarmed into the yamen like ants.

sentences.zh: 一賊號小禁子者，祖德嘗因案懲之，首犯祖德，刃交於胸，被十餘創，罵不絕口，死。

translations.literal: One bandit called Xiaojinzi whom Zude had once punished in a case led the attack on him; blades crossed at his chest, he suffered more than a dozen wounds, cursed without cease, and died.
translations.idiomatic: One rebel nicknamed Xiaojinzi whom Zude had once punished in a case struck first; blades crossed at his chest, he took more than a dozen wounds, cursed without ceasing, and died.

sentences.zh: 守備李大均得訊，躍馬呼殺賊，手無械，不能戰，自經死。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Li Dajun received word, leapt on his horse and cried to kill the bandits. Without a weapon in hand he could not fight and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Li Dajun heard the news, leapt on his horse, and shouted for the rebels to be killed. With no weapon in hand he could not fight and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 於松，漢軍正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Yu Song was a man of the Plain Yellow Banner of the Han Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Song was a Han Bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 以廕授藍翎侍衛，出為江蘇松江糧廳。

translations.literal: Through inherited privilege he was appointed a Blue Feather Bodyguard and went out to serve as grain intendant at Songjiang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Through inherited privilege he was appointed a Blue Feather Bodyguard and went out to serve as grain intendant at Songjiang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 春，南漕改海運，漕船水手將譁變，大吏檄松資遣，變遂定。

translations.literal: That spring the southern tribute grain route was changed to sea transport. The sailors on the grain boats were on the verge of mutiny. The high officials dispatched Song to fund their dismissal, and the mutiny was settled.
translations.idiomatic: That spring the southern tribute route was switched to sea transport. The grain-boat sailors were on the verge of mutiny. The senior officials sent Song to fund their dismissal, and the unrest was settled.

sentences.zh: 明年，大吏復以資遣事檄松，時粵賊已踞江寧為偽都，水手環而嘯呼，勢倍前。

translations.literal: The next year the high officials again dispatched Song on dismissal payments. By then Cantonese bandits had seized Jiangning as their false capital. The sailors gathered round in howling protest, their force twice what it had been before.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the senior officials sent Song on the same dismissal mission again. By then Cantonese rebels had seized Jiangning as their false capital. The sailors crowded round in howling protest, their force twice what it had been before.

sentences.zh: 松為上息內閧計，藉其精壯而訓練之，不旬日，得勁卒二千人。

translations.literal: Song, to still internal strife for the throne, took their strongest men and trained them. Within ten days he had two thousand crack troops.
translations.idiomatic: To quell internal unrest for the throne, Song took their strongest men and trained them. Within ten days he had two thousand crack soldiers.

sentences.zh: 會向榮躡賊圍江寧，江蘇境內稍安。

translations.literal: At that time Xiang Rong was pressing the bandits and besieging Jiangning, and within Jiangsu the situation grew somewhat calm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Rong was then pressing the rebels and besieging Jiangning, and conditions within Jiangsu grew somewhat calmer.

sentences.zh: 六年，率所籍卒從巡撫吉爾杭阿剿鎮江，既成營，搏賊銀山下，戰屢捷。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he led the troops he had enrolled and followed Governor Jierhang'a to suppress Zhenjiang. After the camp was established he fought the bandits at Yinshan below the city and won repeated victories.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he led the troops he had enrolled and followed Governor Jierhang'a against Zhenjiang. Once the camp was established he fought the rebels at Silver Mountain below the city and won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 鎮江賊仰息江寧，既屢創，閉壘，潛略高資鎮。

translations.literal: The bandits at Zhenjiang depended on Jiangning for survival. After repeated defeats they closed their fortifications and secretly raided Gaozi.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels at Zhenjiang depended on Jiangning for their survival. After repeated defeats they shut themselves in their fortifications and secretly raided Gaozi.

sentences.zh: 松以千人馳擊，渡夾江，平賊營。

translations.literal: Song led a thousand men in a rapid attack, crossed Jiajiang, and leveled the bandit camp.
translations.idiomatic: Song led a thousand men in a swift attack, crossed the Jiajiang, and overran the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 改攻鎮江城，以眾夜薄城下，梯垣縱火，潮勇噪而驚賊。

translations.literal: He then turned to assault Zhenjiang city. With his force he drew close to the walls by night, set ladders against the ramparts and kindled fire. The Chaoyong braves raised a clamor and startled the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to assault Zhenjiang itself. At night he brought his force close beneath the walls, raised ladders, and set fires. The Chaoyong braves raised a din and startled the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊起，燃巨砲，登者紛墜。

translations.literal: The bandits rose up, fired great cannon, and those who had scaled the walls fell one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels roused themselves, fired great cannon, and the climbers fell one after another from the walls.

sentences.zh: 松督隊在前，鉛丸中額，僕牙旗下，旋卒。

translations.literal: Song directed his unit from the front. A lead shot struck his forehead and he fell beneath his commander's flag; soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Song led from the front. A musket ball struck his forehead and he fell beneath his commander's flag; he died shortly after.

sentences.zh: 潮勇故剽椎名盜，居嘗啗賊金，故為賊用，敗官軍。

translations.literal: The Chaoyong braves were by nature violent brawlers and notorious bandits. They often took the bandits' gold, and so they served the bandits and routed the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaoyong braves were violent brawlers and notorious bandits by nature. They often took silver from the rebels, so they served the rebels and routed the government troops.

sentences.zh: 松死，麾下士千餘人，悲憤痛哭不忍聞。

translations.literal: When Song died, the more than a thousand soldiers under his command wept in grief and rage beyond bearing to hear.
translations.idiomatic: When Song died, more than a thousand men under his command wept in grief and rage too painful to hear.

sentences.zh: 尚那布，國羅落氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Shang Nabubu was of the Guoluoluo clan, a man of the Bordered Yellow Banner of the Manchus.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Nabubu was of the Guoluoluo clan, a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，由舉人揀發江蘇知縣，八年，署溧陽。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, as a provincial graduate he was selected for appointment as district magistrate in Jiangsu. In the eighth year he served as acting magistrate of Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was selected as a juren for appointment as district magistrate in Jiangsu. In the eighth year he served as acting magistrate of Liyang.

sentences.zh: 僕從蕭然，日集士紳議戰守，不退食。

translations.literal: His attendants were few and spare. Daily he gathered gentry to discuss fighting and holding firm and did not leave his post even for meals.
translations.idiomatic: His staff was sparse. Each day he gathered the gentry to discuss defense and never left his post even to eat.

sentences.zh: 兵勇踐境，親立城卡彈壓，出境乃已。

translations.literal: When soldiers and militia trampled through the district he personally stood at the city checkpoint to suppress them and did not leave until they had crossed the border.
translations.idiomatic: When troops and militia trampled through the district he personally stood at the city checkpoint to keep order and did not stand down until they had left the jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 創義學，築舍數十楹，集諸生講肄，購田百餘畝供膏火。

translations.literal: He founded a charitable school, built several dozen rooms, gathered students for lectures and study, and purchased more than a hundred mu of land to supply lamp-oil stipends.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a charitable school, built several dozen rooms, gathered scholars for lectures and study, and purchased more than a hundred mu of land to fund their stipends.

sentences.zh: 修葺文廟，庀材鳩胥，捐廉為之倡。

translations.literal: He repaired the Confucian temple, gathered materials and labor, and donated from his official salary to lead the effort.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the Confucian temple, gathered materials and labor, and took the lead with a donation from his official salary.

sentences.zh: 疏濬城河，懋遷稱便。

translations.literal: He dredged the city moat, and merchants praised the convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the city moat, and traders praised the convenience.

sentences.zh: 迭以軍需籌防、催徵力最，賞知府銜。

translations.literal: Repeatedly for military supplies, defense planning, and tax collection he exerted himself most strenuously. He was awarded the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Time and again he distinguished himself in provisioning the army, organizing defenses, and collecting taxes. He was awarded the honorary rank of prefect.

sentences.zh: 十年賊陷廣德，溧陽界其北，尚那布誓死守。

translations.literal: In the tenth year bandits captured Guangde. Liyang bordered it to the north, and Shang Nabubu swore to hold the city to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng the rebels took Guangde. Liyang lay on its northern border, and Shang Nabubu vowed to defend the city to the last.

sentences.zh: 賊眾逼城下，急切無援，督練勇擊賊退。

translations.literal: The bandit horde pressed beneath the walls. With no relief at hand, he drilled the militia and drove the bandits back.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces pressed up to the walls. With no help forthcoming, he drilled the militia and beat the rebels back.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊復大集，攻城愈迫，越日城陷。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits gathered again in force and pressed the assault ever harder. The next day the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels massed again and pressed the assault ever harder. The next day the city fell.

sentences.zh: 尚那布厲聲叱曰：「我溧陽知縣，練勇殺賊，我作主，速殺我，勿傷百姓！」

translations.literal: Shang Nabubu shouted sternly: "I am the magistrate of Liyang. The militia killed bandits at my command. Kill me quickly and do not harm the people!"
translations.idiomatic: Shang Nabubu shouted in a thunderous voice: "I am the magistrate of Liyang. The militia killed rebels at my order. Strike me down at once—do not harm the people!"

sentences.zh: 遂遇害。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was slain.

sentences.zh: 卹贈太僕寺卿銜，賞世職。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was awarded the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 時署金壇縣知縣李淮同以城陷殉難。

translations.literal: At the time Li Huaitong, acting magistrate of Jintan, likewise died defending the city when it fell.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Li Huaitong, acting magistrate of Jintan, also perished defending his city when it fell.

sentences.zh: 淮，字小石，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Huai, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huai, courtesy name Xiaoshi, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 固守至百餘日，賊乘霧登城，淮朝服坐堂皇，罵賊死之。

translations.literal: He held firm for more than a hundred days. The bandits scaled the walls in fog. Huai sat in court robes in the main hall, cursed the bandits, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He held out for more than a hundred days. The rebels scaled the walls in the fog. Huai sat in his court robes in the main hall, cursed the rebels, and died.

sentences.zh: 唐治，字魯泉，江蘇句容人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhi, courtesy name Luquan, was a native of Jurong, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhi, courtesy name Luquan, was a native of Jurong in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光五年舉人，大挑知縣，分安徽，補桐城縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination, was selected as magistrate through the special appointment, was assigned to Anhui, and was appointed magistrate of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination, was selected for appointment as magistrate, was assigned to Anhui, and took up the post of magistrate of Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 歲大水，請帑勸分，按口賑施，不假手胥吏，一月鬚髮為白。

translations.literal: That year great floods struck. He requested treasury funds and urged private contributions, distributing relief by head count without delegating to clerks. Within a month his beard and hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: That year catastrophic floods struck. He secured treasury funds and urged private contributions, distributing relief by head count without leaving the work to clerks. Within a month his hair had turned white.

sentences.zh: 調祁門，舊有東山書院，生童膏火取給鹽釐，治別籌捐項充經費，士商兩便之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qimen. The old Dongshan Academy there had relied on salt levies for students' stipends. Zhi raised separate donations to cover the expenses, to the convenience of scholars and merchants alike.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qimen. The old Dongshan Academy there had drawn students' stipends from salt levies. Zhi raised separate donations to cover the costs, to the benefit of scholars and merchants alike.

sentences.zh: 又立義廒，積穀至數万石。

translations.literal: He also established a charitable granary and accumulated grain to tens of thousands of shi.
translations.idiomatic: He also established a charitable granary and stockpiled tens of thousands of shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 時粵賊據江寧，安徽改省治廬州，賊船上下無所忌。

translations.literal: At the time the Cantonese bandits held Jiangning. Anhui moved its provincial seat to Luzhou, and the bandit boats moved up and down the river without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Taiping rebels held Nanjing. Anhui had moved its provincial seat to Luzhou, and rebel boats moved freely up and down the river.

sentences.zh: 上書陳利害，不報；

translations.literal: He submitted memorials setting forth the advantages and dangers, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted memorials detailing the dangers of the situation, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 祁門無兵，依山為城，徽州以富名，賊欲圖徽，必道祁，請以兵守，又不報；

translations.literal: Qimen had no troops. Its walls ran along the mountains. Huizhou was famed for wealth, and the bandits intended to seize it and would have to pass through Qimen. He requested troops for its defense, but again received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Qimen had no garrison. Its walls clung to the mountains. Huizhou was renowned for its wealth, and the rebels, intending to seize it, would have to pass through Qimen. He requested troops to hold the place, but again received no reply.

sentences.zh: 而祁之奸民前苦治嚴緝者，遂為賊鄉道。

translations.literal: The disreputable men of Qimen who had suffered under his strict enforcement now served the bandits as guides.
translations.idiomatic: The local ruffians of Qimen, who had chafed under his strict enforcement, now guided the rebels into the district.

sentences.zh: 道光四年正月，賊入縣屬櫸根嶺，治招集團丁，激以大義，誓共城存亡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Daoguang, bandits entered Jungen Ridge in the county's jurisdiction. Zhi gathered the militia, roused them with the call of duty, and swore to share the city's fate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year of Daoguang, rebels entered Jungen Ridge within the county. Zhi gathered the militia, roused them with the call of duty, and swore to live or die with the city.

sentences.zh: 時大洪司巡檢鍾普塘亦帶勇入城協守，賊偪西門，治督眾登陴迎戰，砲轟斃匪數十人。

translations.literal: At the time Zhong Putang, assistant inspector of Dahong Subprefecture, also led militia into the city to help defend it. The bandits pressed the west gate. Zhi led the men onto the battlements to meet them. Cannon fire killed dozens of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhong Putang, assistant inspector of Dahong Subprefecture, also led militiamen into the city to help defend it. The rebels pressed the west gate. Zhi led his men onto the battlements to meet them, and cannon fire killed dozens of rebels.

sentences.zh: 大股猝至，城遂陷，猶奮勇巷戰，力竭馬蹶，與普塘同時被執。

translations.literal: A large force arrived suddenly and the city fell. He still fought fiercely in the lanes until strength failed and his horse stumbled. He and Putang were seized at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: A large force arrived without warning and the city fell. He still fought fiercely in the streets until his strength gave out and his horse stumbled. He and Putang were captured together.

sentences.zh: 誘降不可，凌辱之，不屈，以禮遇之，終不食飲，卒罵賊死。

translations.literal: They tried to win him over, but he would not submit. They humiliated him, but he would not yield. They then treated him with courtesy, yet he still would not eat or drink, and in the end cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to win him over, but he refused. They humiliated him, but he would not bend. They then treated him with courtesy, yet he still would not eat or drink, and in the end cursed the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 普塘同時遇害，沉屍於河。

translations.literal: Putang was killed at the same time, and his body was thrown into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Putang was killed at the same time, and his body was cast into the river.

sentences.zh: 普塘，紹興人。

translations.literal: Putang was a native of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Putang was a native of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 賊欲說降之，曰：「吾年逾六十矣，即不知羞恥事，能再活六十餘耶？」

translations.literal: When the bandits tried to persuade him to surrender, he said: "I am already more than sixty years old. Even if I were shameless enough to submit, could I live another sixty years?"
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels tried to persuade him to surrender, he said: "I am already past sixty. Even if I were shameless enough to submit, could I live another sixty years?"

sentences.zh: 傳其罵賊尤烈雲，

translations.literal: It is said that his curses against the bandits were especially fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition holds that his curses against the rebels were especially fierce.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓請於祁門建專祠，以鍾普塘附祀。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan requested a dedicated shrine at Qimen, with Zhong Putang enshrined alongside.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan requested a dedicated shrine at Qimen, with Zhong Putang enshrined alongside him.

sentences.zh: 賊躪安徽，守土吏殉節死者，又有泗州知州鄭沅，六安州知州金寶樹，蒙城縣知縣宋維屏，望江縣知縣衛君選，盱眙縣知縣許垣。

translations.literal: As the bandits ravaged Anhui, other local officials who died defending their posts included Zheng Yuan, prefect of Sizhou; Jin Baoshu, prefect of Lu'an; Song Weiping, magistrate of Mengcheng; Wei Junxuan, magistrate of Wangjiang; and Xu Yuan, magistrate of Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels ravaged Anhui, other local officials who died defending their posts included Zheng Yuan, prefect of Sizhou; Jin Baoshu, prefect of Lu'an; Song Weiping, magistrate of Mengcheng; Wei Junxuan, magistrate of Wangjiang; and Xu Yuan, magistrate of Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 沅，順天大興人；

translations.literal: Yuan was a native of Daxing, Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 寶樹，江蘇元和人；

translations.literal: Baoshu was a native of Yuanhe, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Baoshu was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 君選，河南趙城人；

translations.literal: Junxuan was a native of Zhaocheng, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Junxuan was a native of Zhaocheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 垣，江蘇上元人；

translations.literal: Yuan was a native of Shangyuan, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was a native of Shangyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 維屏籍未詳。

translations.literal: Weiping's native place is not recorded in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Weiping's place of origin is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 林源恩，字秀三，四川達州人。

translations.literal: Lin Yuan'en, courtesy name Xiusan, was a native of Dazhou, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yuan'en, courtesy name Xiusan, was a native of Dazhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 拔貢生。

translations.literal: He was a selected tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He was a selected tribute student.

sentences.zh: 舉順天鄉試，咸豐元年，選湖南平江縣知縣。

translations.literal: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination. In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed magistrate of Pingjiang County, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Shuntian provincial examination. In the first year of Xianfeng he was appointed magistrate of Pingjiang County in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，粵賊犯長沙，瀏陽、通城匪徒皆為亂，三縣皆與平江接壤。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year the Cantonese bandits attacked Changsha. Ruffians in Liuyang and Tongcheng rose in revolt. All three counties bordered Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year the Taiping rebels attacked Changsha. Ruffians in Liuyang and Tongcheng rose in revolt. All three counties bordered Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 源恩詰姦守隘，如防禦水，截然不得蟄。

translations.literal: Yuan'en interrogated traitors and guarded the passes as if defending against floodwater, allowing no breach whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'en interrogated traitors and guarded the passes as if holding back a flood, allowing no breach whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 江忠源以為才，保奏知州銜​​，又以書播告士友，道「林某堪軍旅」也。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan regarded him as talented, memorialized the throne recommending him for the rank of prefect, and also wrote to his scholarly friends declaring that "Lin is fit for military command."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhongyuan regarded him as talented, memorialized the throne recommending him for the rank of prefect, and also wrote to his scholarly friends declaring that "Lin is fit for military command."

sentences.zh: 時曾國籓治兵長沙，檄源恩募平江勇五百人以從。

translations.literal: At the time Zeng Guofan was raising troops at Changsha and ordered Yuan'en to recruit five hundred Pingjiang militiamen to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zeng Guofan was raising troops at Changsha and ordered Yuan'en to recruit five hundred Pingjiang militiamen to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 旋有他賊自崇陽、通城犯平江，檄源恩回援，壁北鄉之上塔市。

translations.literal: Soon other bandits from Chongyang and Tongcheng invaded Pingjiang. Yuan'en was ordered back to relieve the county and entrenched at Shangtashi in the northern township.
translations.idiomatic: Soon other rebels from Chongyang and Tongcheng invaded Pingjiang. Yuan'en was ordered back to relieve the county and entrenched at Shangtashi in the northern township.

sentences.zh: 三月四日，賊大至，環源恩壘，源恩逆戰，大捷，追奔數十里。

translations.literal: On the fourth day of the third month the bandits arrived in force and encircled Yuan'en's camp. Yuan'en met them in battle and won a great victory, pursuing the fugitives for dozens of li.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth day of the third month the rebels arrived in force and encircled Yuan'en's camp. Yuan'en met them in battle and won a great victory, pursuing the fugitives for dozens of li.

sentences.zh: 既而塔齊布、胡林翼師克通城，平江解嚴，師別剿，則賊仍麕至，源恩屢戰卻之。

translations.literal: Later Taqibuy and Hu Linyi's army captured Tongcheng, Pingjiang's alarm was lifted, and the army marched off on other campaigns. Then bandits swarmed in again, and Yuan'en repeatedly fought them off.
translations.idiomatic: Later the army under Taqibuy and Hu Linyi captured Tongcheng, the alarm in Pingjiang was lifted, and the army marched off on other campaigns. Then rebels swarmed in again, and Yuan'en repeatedly drove them back.

sentences.zh: 會有忌源恩者，功不得敘，又別摭他事中之。

translations.literal: But there were those who envied Yuan'en, so his merits went unrewarded, and others seized on other matters to bring accusations against him.
translations.idiomatic: But there were those who envied Yuan'en, so his merits went unrewarded, and others seized on other matters to bring accusations against him.

sentences.zh: 源恩憤甚，詣大府自陳，而謇於辭，卒莫能自達。

translations.literal: Yuan'en was deeply indignant. He went to the provincial governor to plead his case, but he was awkward in speech and in the end could not make himself understood.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'en was deeply indignant. He went to the provincial governor to plead his case, but he was halting in speech and in the end could not make himself understood.

sentences.zh: 遂從國籓九江軍，命治羅澤南糧台。

translations.literal: He then followed Guofan's army at Jiujiang and was ordered to manage Luo Zemin's supply depot.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Guofan's army at Jiujiang and was ordered to manage Luo Zemin's supply depot.

sentences.zh: 乙卯春，從克廣信，賞花翎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the yimao year he followed the campaign to capture Guangxin and was awarded a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the yimao year he took part in the capture of Guangxin and was awarded a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 又治塔齊布糧台，旋任水師營務。

translations.literal: He again managed Taqibuy's supply depot and soon took charge of naval camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He again managed Taqibuy's supply depot and soon took charge of naval camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 十一月，又攝理陸軍於廬山之麓、姑塘之南，而江西巡撫聞源恩賢，飛檄至南昌，付以所新募之平江營者。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he also acted in command of the land army at the foot of Mount Lu and south of Gufang. The Jiangxi governor, hearing that Yuan'en was worthy, sent an urgent dispatch to Nanchang entrusting him with the newly recruited Pingjiang Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he also acted in command of the land army at the foot of Mount Lu and south of Gufang. The Jiangxi governor, hearing that Yuan'en was a man of talent, sent an urgent dispatch to Nanchang entrusting him with the newly recruited Pingjiang Battalion.

sentences.zh: 源恩在廬山，又與共事武夫不相能，憤彌甚，嘗獨歎曰：「丈夫一死強寇耳，終不返顧矣！」

translations.literal: At Mount Lu Yuan'en again could not get along with the military men serving with him. His anger grew ever fiercer, and once he sighed alone: "A man need only die fighting fierce bandits and never look back!"
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Lu Yuan'en again could not get along with the military men serving alongside him. His anger grew ever fiercer, and once he sighed alone: "A man need only die fighting fierce rebels—and never look back!"

sentences.zh: 明年，石達開犯江西，連陷八府五十餘州縣。

translations.literal: The next year Shi Dakai invaded Jiangxi and in succession captured more than fifty prefectures and counties in eight circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Shi Dakai invaded Jiangxi and in succession captured more than fifty prefectures and counties across eight circuits.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，李元度率師自湖口南來，源恩與鄧輔綸自南昌而東，兩軍會於撫州，克進賢東鄉，進破文昌橋堅壘五，赭其巢。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year Li Yuandu led his army south from Hukou. Yuan'en and Deng Fuzun marched east from Nanchang. The two armies met at Fuzhou, captured Jinxian and Dongxiang, advanced and broke five strong fortifications at Wenchang Bridge, and burned out their nests.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the sixth year Li Yuandu led his army south from Hukou. Yuan'en and Deng Fuzun marched east from Nanchang. The two armies met at Fuzhou, captured Jinxian and Dongxiang, advanced and broke five strong fortifications at Wenchang Bridge, and burned out their strongholds.

sentences.zh: 既薄城，源恩壁南門，元度壁西南隅，相去四里。

translations.literal: When they drew near the city, Yuan'en encamped at the south gate and Yuandu at the southwest corner, four li apart.
translations.idiomatic: When they drew near the city, Yuan'en encamped at the south gate and Yuandu at the southwest corner, four li apart.

sentences.zh: 賊嬰城拒守，堅不可拔。

translations.literal: The bandits held the city and resisted. It could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held the city and resisted. It could not be taken.

sentences.zh: 當是時，江、楚道梗，瑞、臨、袁、吉四郡無一官軍。

translations.literal: At that time the routes between Jiangxi and Huguang were blocked, and in the four prefectures of Rui, Lin, Yuan, and Ji there was not a single government army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the routes between Jiangxi and Huguang were cut off, and in the four prefectures of Rui, Lin, Yuan, and Ji there was not a single government army.

sentences.zh: 援賊不時至，​​至則合城賊來犯，所部迎擊三十里外，輒重創之，破賊壘者九，大小戰五十有六，皆告捷。

translations.literal: Relief bandits arrived from time to time, and whenever they came they joined the city bandits in attack. Yuan'en's troops met them thirty li outside the walls and always inflicted heavy losses, breaking nine bandit camps. In fifty-six engagements large and small, all ended in victory.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements arrived from time to time, and whenever they came they joined the defenders in attacking the besiegers. Yuan'en's troops met them thirty li outside the walls and always inflicted heavy losses, breaking nine rebel camps. In fifty-six engagements large and small, all ended in victory.

sentences.zh: 然部下血戰久，疲不得休，裹創者十之三，病者十四五。

translations.literal: Yet his men had fought in blood for a long time, weary and unable to rest. One in three wrapped wounds; one in four or five were ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his men had fought in blood for a long time, weary and unable to rest. One in three bore bandaged wounds; one in four or five were sick.

sentences.zh: 會輔綸中蜚語去，在事者多告退，源恩勢益孤，餉日絀。

translations.literal: Then Fuzun fell victim to slander and left. Many of those in the field resigned. Yuan'en's position grew ever more isolated, and supplies daily ran short.
translations.idiomatic: Then Fuzun fell victim to slander and withdrew. Many of those in the field resigned. Yuan'en's position grew ever more isolated, and supplies daily ran short.

sentences.zh: 宜黃、崇仁兩縣來乞師，謂克宜、崇則能拊撫賊之背，且勸士民輸餉，可得十數万。

translations.literal: The two counties of Yihuang and Chongren came begging for troops, saying that if Yihuang and Chongren were taken they could strike the bandits in the rear, and that by urging the gentry and people to supply provisions they could obtain one or two hundred thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: The two counties of Yihuang and Chongren came begging for troops, saying that if Yihuang and Chongren were taken they could strike the rebels in the rear, and that by urging the gentry and people to supply provisions they could raise one or two hundred thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 源恩與元度遂分江、楚軍共五千徇西路。

translations.literal: Yuan'en and Yuandu then divided the Jiang-Hu army, five thousand strong, to advance along the western route.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'en and Yuandu then divided the Jiang-Hu army, five thousand strong, to advance along the western route.

sentences.zh: 九月三日，克宜黃，九日，克崇仁，俘斬各數百。

translations.literal: On the third day of the ninth month they captured Yihuang. On the ninth day they captured Chongren, taking and killing several hundred in each place.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the ninth month they captured Yihuang. On the ninth day they captured Chongren, taking and killing several hundred in each place.

sentences.zh: 忽皖賊數千自景德鎮來援，急撤宜、崇軍，官民苦留不遣。

translations.literal: Suddenly several thousand bandits from Anhui came from Jingdezhen to relieve the siege. They hurriedly withdrew the Yihuang and Chongren armies, but officials and people bitterly pleaded that they not be sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly several thousand rebels from Anhui came from Jingdezhen to relieve the siege. They hurriedly withdrew the Yihuang and Chongren armies, but officials and people bitterly pleaded that they not be sent away.

sentences.zh: 將士亦以久飢甫得一飽，不能行。

translations.literal: The officers and men too, having been long hungry and only just having had one full meal, could not march.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men too, having gone hungry for so long and only just having had one full meal, could not march.

sentences.zh: 賊趨撫州，十六日，扼河而戰。

translations.literal: The bandits pressed toward Fuzhou. On the sixteenth day they fought with the river at their back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed toward Fuzhou. On the sixteenth day they fought with the river at their back.

sentences.zh: 水涸，賊駷馬飛渡，追而敗諸城下。

translations.literal: The water had dried up. The bandits galloped across at a flying pace, pursued them, and defeated them beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The river had run dry. The rebels galloped across at full speed, pursued them, and defeated them beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 先是源恩所部之右護軍遣赴崇仁，留三百人守壘，賊诇知之，詰旦出犯，先陷右軍，遂圍源恩壁。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuan'en's Right Guard Army had been sent to Chongren, leaving three hundred men to hold the camp. The bandits learned this by espionage. At dawn they sallied forth to attack, first overthrowing the right army, then encircling Yuan'en's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuan'en's Right Guard Army had been sent to Chongren, leaving three hundred men to hold the camp. The rebels learned this through spies. At dawn they sallied forth to attack, first overthrowing the right army, then encircling Yuan'en's camp.

sentences.zh: 源恩慷慨諭將士曰：「好男子，努力殺賊，無走也！」

translations.literal: Yuan'en addressed the officers and men with generous spirit: "Good men, strive hard to kill bandits. Do not flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'en addressed the officers and men with generous spirit: "Good men, strive hard to kill the rebels. Do not flee!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆應曰：「惟公命。」

translations.literal: All answered: "We obey your command alone."
translations.idiomatic: All answered: "We obey your command alone."

sentences.zh: 都司唐德昇馳入壁，掖源恩上馬，源恩曰：「此吾死所也，子受事日淺，其行乎！」

translations.literal: Battalion commander Tang Desheng galloped into the camp, helped Yuan'en mount a horse. Yuan'en said: "This is where I die. You have served only a short time—go!"
translations.idiomatic: Battalion commander Tang Desheng galloped into the camp and helped Yuan'en mount a horse. Yuan'en said: "This is where I die. You have served only a short time—go!"

sentences.zh: 德昇曰：「君能死，吾獨不能死耶？」

translations.literal: Desheng said: "If you can die, can I alone not die?"
translations.idiomatic: Desheng said: "If you can die, can I alone not die?"

sentences.zh: 從容解金條脫畀其從子某，曰：「若馳去，吾與林公死此矣！」

translations.literal: Calmly he removed a gold ingot and handed it to a certain nephew, saying: "You ride off. I and Master Lin will die here!"
translations.idiomatic: Calmly he removed a gold ingot and handed it to a nephew, saying: "You ride off. I and Master Lin will die here!"

sentences.zh: 壘破，源恩手劍鏦賊，力竭，死之。

translations.literal: The camp was broken. Yuan'en took sword in hand and thrust at the bandits until strength failed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The camp was overrun. Yuan'en took sword in hand and thrust at the rebels until his strength failed and he died.

sentences.zh: 德昇素驍健，格殺十餘賊，始被害。

translations.literal: Desheng was by nature fierce and strong. He killed more than ten bandits in close combat before he too was slain.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng was by nature fierce and strong. He killed more than ten rebels in close combat before he too was slain.

sentences.zh: 從死者三百餘人。

translations.literal: More than three hundred died with them.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred died with them.

sentences.zh: 源恩年僅四十。

translations.literal: Yuan'en was only forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan'en was only forty years old.

sentences.zh: 追贈道員，賜卹如例。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was promoted to circuit intendant and granted mourning stipends according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was promoted to circuit intendant and granted mourning stipends according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 德昇，字彥遠，寧遠人。

translations.literal: Desheng, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a native of Ningyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Desheng, courtesy name Yanyuan, was a native of Ningyuan.

sentences.zh: 舊隸副將周鳳山部下，以十五日奉檄來軍，十七日及難，贈游擊。

translations.literal: He had formerly served under Vice General Zhou Fengshan. On the fifteenth he received orders to join the army; on the seventeenth he met disaster. Posthumously he was awarded the rank of guerrilla colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He had formerly served under Vice General Zhou Fengshan. On the fifteenth he received orders to join the army; on the seventeenth he met disaster. Posthumously he was awarded the rank of guerrilla colonel.

sentences.zh: 畢大鈺，湖南長沙人，

translations.literal: Bi Dayu was a native of Changsha, Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Dayu was a native of Changsha in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 以附生守長沙南關，粵賊砲轟城塌，大鈺斂空棺實土為牆，頃刻成三十餘丈。

translations.literal: As a supplemental licentiate he defended the south gate of Changsha. Cantonese bandit cannon fire breached the wall. Dayu gathered empty coffins, filled them with earth to make a wall, and in an instant completed more than thirty zhang.
translations.idiomatic: As a supplemental licentiate he defended the south gate of Changsha. Taiping cannon fire breached the wall. Dayu gathered empty coffins, filled them with earth to build a wall, and in an instant completed more than thirty zhang.

sentences.zh: 隨提督鄧紹良堅拒八十餘日，殲賊數千。

translations.literal: Following Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang he held firm for more than eighty days and destroyed several thousand bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Following Grand Coordinator Deng Shaoliang he held firm for more than eighty days and destroyed several thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊自湖北迴竄，湘潭、靖港均陷，大鈺復以防省功選用府經歷、縣丞。

translations.literal: When bandits doubled back from Hubei, Xiangtan and Jinggang both fell. Dayu was again selected for appointment as prefectural secretary and assistant magistrate for his services in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels doubled back from Hubei, Xiangtan and Jinggang both fell. Dayu was again selected for appointment as prefectural secretary and assistant magistrate for his services in defense.

sentences.zh: 湖北崇陽、通城陷，大鈺复領兵赴剿。

translations.literal: When Chongyang and Tongcheng in Hubei fell, Dayu again led troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyang and Tongcheng in Hubei fell, Dayu again led troops to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 諜知賊由平江搗長沙，絕饋道，厲兵為備，賊不得逞。

translations.literal: By espionage he learned that bandits would strike Changsha by way of Pingjiang and cut the supply route. He hardened his troops and made ready, and the bandits could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Through spies he learned that rebels would strike Changsha by way of Pingjiang and cut the supply route. He hardened his troops and made ready, and the rebels could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 行軍禁騷擾，一蔬一木無妄取。

translations.literal: On campaign he forbade harassment. Not a vegetable or tree was taken without cause.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign he forbade harassment. Not a vegetable or tree was taken without cause.

sentences.zh: 通城亂久無官，為立團防，鋤土匪，通人安業。

translations.literal: Tongcheng had long been in disorder with no officials. He established militia defense, uprooted bandits, and the people of Tongcheng lived in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tongcheng had long been in disorder with no officials. He established militia defense, uprooted bandits, and the people of Tongcheng lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 因其歸，報金巨萬，大鈺卻不受。

translations.literal: Because of his return they offered him a gift of tens of thousands of taels of gold, but Dayu refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In gratitude for his return they offered him a gift of tens of thousands of taels of gold, but Dayu refused to accept it.

sentences.zh: 四年，保用知縣，授浙江仙居知縣，案無留牘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recommended for appointment as magistrate and was appointed magistrate of Xianju, Zhejiang. No case lingered on his desk.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recommended for appointment as magistrate and was appointed magistrate of Xianju in Zhejiang. No case lingered on his desk.

sentences.zh: 地瘠民貧，逋賦多，大鈺在官，民爭輸納。

translations.literal: The land was poor and the people impoverished, and tax arrears were many. While Dayu held office the people competed to pay their dues.
translations.idiomatic: The land was poor and the people impoverished, and tax arrears were many. While Dayu held office the people competed to pay their dues.

sentences.zh: 尋捐知府，浙江巡撫何桂清留筦糧台，檄赴於潛防堵。

translations.literal: Soon he purchased the rank of prefect. Zhejiang Governor He Guiqing kept him to manage the supply depot and ordered him to Yuqian for blocking operations.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he purchased the rank of prefect. Zhejiang Governor He Guiqing kept him to manage the supply depot and ordered him to Yuqian for blocking operations.

sentences.zh: 又以開化疊警，調防婺源。

translations.literal: Because Kaihua was repeatedly alarmed, he was transferred to defend Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kaihua was repeatedly alarmed, he was transferred to defend Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 初戰屢捷，尋賊以三千人圍南關，大鈺偕胞侄候選通判榮清合剿，賊大至，力竭，均死之。

translations.literal: At first he won repeated victories. Then bandits with three thousand men besieged the south gate. Dayu, together with his younger cousin, candidate vice prefect Rong Qing, joined in a combined attack. The bandits arrived in force. Strength failed and both died.
translations.idiomatic: At first he won repeated victories. Then rebels with three thousand men besieged the south gate. Dayu, together with his younger cousin, candidate vice prefect Rong Qing, joined in a combined attack. The rebels arrived in force. Their strength failed and both died.

sentences.zh: 卹贈太僕寺卿，賞世職。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was awarded the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Stud and granted a hereditary office.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was awarded the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and granted a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 湯世銓，字彥聲，順天大興籍，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Tang Shiquan, courtesy name Yansheng, registered in Daxing, Shuntian, was a native of Wujin, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shiquan, courtesy name Yansheng, was registered in Daxing, Shuntian, though a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 舉人，

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 以知縣發浙江，七年，署開化縣。

translations.literal: He was dispatched to Zhejiang as magistrate. In the seventh year he served as acting magistrate of Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to Zhejiang as magistrate. In the seventh year he served as acting magistrate of Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪闌入浙境，由常山窺開化，委署者多不肯往，世銓獨毅然請行，至則募勇防守。

translations.literal: At the time Cantonese bandits had broken into Zhejiang from Changshan and were eyeing Kaihua. Many of those appointed to acting posts refused to go. Shiquan alone resolutely volunteered. When he arrived he recruited militia for defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taiping rebels had broken into Zhejiang from Changshan and were eyeing Kaihua. Many of those appointed to acting posts refused to go. Shiquan alone resolutely volunteered. When he arrived he recruited militia for defense.

sentences.zh: 八年三月，賊首石達開擾浙，衢州鎮總兵饒廷選戰敗，遂偪開化。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year the bandit chieftain Shi Dakai harassed Zhejiang. Rao Tingxuan, regional commander at Quzhou, was defeated in battle, and the rebels then pressed Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year the rebel chieftain Shi Dakai harassed Zhejiang. Rao Tingxuan, regional commander at Quzhou, was defeated in battle, and the rebels then pressed Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 世銓聞警登陴，賊突至，城陷，世銓拔佩刀自剄，為紳民奪刀擁出，不得死。

translations.literal: Shiquan, hearing the alarm, mounted the battlements. The bandits burst in suddenly and the city fell. Shiquan drew his sword to cut his throat, but gentry and people seized the blade and dragged him out, so he could not die.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan, hearing the alarm, mounted the battlements. The rebels burst in suddenly and the city fell. Shiquan drew his sword to cut his throat, but gentry and people seized the blade and dragged him out, so he could not die.

sentences.zh: 陰約各都結團，且飛書請兵，會鶴麗鎮總兵週天孚督軍追擊，賊奔處州，世銓率團沿途截殺。

translations.literal: Secretly he arranged for each district to form militia units, and sent urgent dispatches requesting troops. At that time Zhou Tianfu, regional commander at Heli, supervised the army in pursuit. The bandits fled toward Chuzhou, and Shiquan led the militia units in intercepting and killing them along the way.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he arranged for each district to form militia units and sent urgent dispatches requesting reinforcements. Regional commander Zhou Tianfu of Heli led troops in pursuit, and the rebels fled toward Chuzhou. Shiquan led the militia units in intercepting and killing them along the route.

sentences.zh: 六月，縣城复，仍因失守褫職，代未至，仍帶勇守禦。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the county seat was recovered. He was still stripped of office for having lost the city, but his replacement had not yet arrived, so he continued to lead militia in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the county seat was recovered. Though still stripped of office for the fall of the city, his replacement had not yet arrived, so he continued to lead militia in the defense.

sentences.zh: 七月，賊由常山復攻開化，江蘇候補知縣劉福林帥鄉勇方檄赴寧國。

translations.literal: In the seventh month bandits again attacked Kaihua from Changshan. Liu Fulin, candidate magistrate of Jiangsu, was leading local militia and had just received orders to proceed to Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the rebels again attacked Kaihua from Changshan. Liu Fulin, a candidate magistrate from Jiangsu, was leading local militia and had just received orders to proceed to Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 世銓請於大府，留籍防禦，而以城守囑縣丞某，且出印印其衣，畢，遣人賚印至府授代者，遂出禦賊於華埠。

translations.literal: Shiquan petitioned the provincial authorities to remain locally for defense. He entrusted city defense to a certain assistant magistrate, and furthermore produced the seal to stamp his clothing. When finished, he sent someone to carry the seal to the prefecture to deliver to his successor, then went out to meet the bandits at Huabu.
translations.idiomatic: Shiquan petitioned the provincial authorities to remain and defend the area. He entrusted the city walls to an assistant magistrate, stamped his official seal on his clothing, and sent an envoy to deliver the seal to his successor at the prefectural seat. Then he went out to meet the rebels at Huabu.

sentences.zh: 賊至，疊擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the bandits arrived he repeatedly struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived he repeatedly struck and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 會貴州定遠協副將硃貴統兵三千夾援，戰失利，世銓急整隊出，倉猝不能成陣，力鬥，與福林同歿於戰所。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Gui, assistant regional commander of the Dingyuan Brigade in Guizhou, led three thousand troops in a converging relief. The battle went badly. Shiquan hurriedly formed his ranks and went out, but in the haste could not form proper formation. Fighting with all his strength, he perished on the field together with Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhu Gui, assistant regional commander of the Dingyuan Brigade in Guizhou, brought three thousand troops in converging relief. The battle went against them. Shiquan hurriedly rallied his men and went out, but in the rush could not form proper lines. Fighting with all his strength, he fell on the field together with Fulin.

sentences.zh: 以印衣覓得屍，胸腹腰肋創十數。

translations.literal: By the stamped clothing they found his corpse. He had more than ten wounds on chest, belly, waist, and ribs.
translations.idiomatic: His body was identified by the stamped clothing. His chest, belly, waist, and ribs bore more than ten wounds.

sentences.zh: 勇目方忠同死於其側。

translations.literal: The militia squad leader Fang Zhong died at his side.
translations.idiomatic: The militia squad leader Fang Zhong died at his side.

sentences.zh: 事聞，復原官，卹如例，給世職。

translations.literal: When report reached the court his original office was restored, mourning stipends were granted according to regulation, and a hereditary office was given.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court his original rank was restored, he received mourning stipends according to regulation, and a hereditary office was granted.

sentences.zh: 謝子澄，字云航，四川新都人。

translations.literal: Xie Zicheng, courtesy name Yunhang, was a native of Xindu, Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zicheng, courtesy name Yunhang, was a native of Xindu in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 舉人，大挑知縣，分直隸。

translations.literal: He was a provincial graduate, selected in the grand nomination for magistrate, and assigned to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate, he was selected in the grand nomination for magistrate and assigned to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，署無極縣，二年，補天津。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Wuji. In the second year he was appointed to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Wuji. In the second year he was appointed to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 天津地濱海，獷悍難治，市有所謂「混混」者，健武善鬥。

translations.literal: Tianjin lay by the sea; the people were fierce and hard to govern. In the market were those called "hunhun"—robust and skilled in fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin lay by the sea, and its people were fierce and hard to govern. In the markets were men known as "hunhun"—hardy brawlers skilled in fighting.

sentences.zh: 子澄至，見前令系諸混混，歎曰：「是奚不可化者？」

translations.literal: When Zicheng arrived he saw the previous magistrate had imprisoned the various hunhun. He sighed and said: "Are these men beyond reform?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zicheng arrived he saw the previous magistrate had imprisoned the various hunhun. He sighed and said: "Are these men beyond reform?"

sentences.zh: 籍其名，縱之。

translations.literal: He registered their names and released them.
translations.idiomatic: He registered their names and released them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，縱者閧於市，子澄按名捕，殛其魁，地面遂靖。

translations.literal: Before long the released men raised a disturbance in the market. Zicheng arrested them by name and executed their ringleader, and the district was soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the released men raised a disturbance in the market. Zicheng arrested them by name, executed their ringleader, and the district was soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪出擾湘、漢，順流而東，遣酋林鳳祥、李開芳分兵渡河，莫測所向。

translations.literal: At the time Cantonese bandits raided out of Hunan and the Han region, flowing east downstream. They sent chieftains Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang to divide troops and cross the river. No one could discern where they would go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Taiping rebels raided through Hunan and the Han region, flowing east along the river. They sent chieftains Lin Fengxiang and Li Kaifang to divide their forces and cross north. No one could tell where they would strike next.

sentences.zh: 人方謂南北道隔，賊不敢犯，子澄深以為憂。

translations.literal: People were just saying the northern and southern routes were cut off and the bandits would not dare invade. Zicheng was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: People were saying the routes north and south were cut off and the rebels would not dare invade. Zicheng was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 捐金倡團練，召所縱諸混混，以周處故事喻之，眾皆為用。

translations.literal: He donated money to sponsor militia training, summoned the various hunhun he had released, and used the story of Zhou Chu to instruct them. All came to serve.
translations.idiomatic: He donated money to sponsor militia training, called up the various hunhun he had released, and used the tale of Zhou Chu to instruct them. All came to serve.

sentences.zh: 回民劉繼德复集回民千餘人應之，遂率赴教場，授器械，教戰陣之法，其妻亦撤簪珥以助。

translations.literal: The Hui Muslim Liu Jide in turn gathered more than a thousand Hui to respond. Thereupon he led them to the drill ground, supplied weapons, and taught methods of battle formation. His wife also removed her hairpins and earrings to assist.
translations.idiomatic: The Hui Muslim Liu Jide in turn rallied more than a thousand Hui to answer the call. He led them to the drill ground, supplied weapons, and taught battle formations. His wife also removed her hairpins and earrings to help.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽政文謙歸財與糧，隨時協濟，子澄得一意練兵。

translations.literal: Wen Qian, salt commissioner of Changlu, contributed funds and grain, assisting at all times. Zicheng could then concentrate entirely on drilling troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qian, the Changlu salt commissioner, supplied funds and grain whenever needed. Zicheng was thus able to concentrate entirely on drilling troops.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊圍懷慶。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits besieged Huaiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels besieged Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 踰月，渡臨洺關，總督納爾經額帥師遁，遂經順河、柏鄉、欒城入深州。

translations.literal: After more than a month they crossed Linming Pass. Governor-General Nayanceng led the army in flight, and the bandits passed through Sunhe, Baixiang, and Luancheng, entering Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month they crossed Linming Pass. Governor-General Nayanceng fled with his army, and the rebels passed through Sunhe, Baixiang, and Luancheng into Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 主閫者務持重，雖數奉詔夾剿，而習於潰逃，數避賊。

translations.literal: Those in supreme command sought to be cautious. Although repeatedly ordered by imperial edict to attack from both sides, they were accustomed to breaking and fleeing and often avoided the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The supreme commanders sought to play it safe. Although repeatedly ordered by imperial edict to attack from both sides, they were accustomed to breaking and fleeing and often avoided the rebels.

sentences.zh: 其奮勇者尾追數千里，氣亦餒，賊勢益橫。

translations.literal: Those who fought bravely pursued tails for several thousand li, but their spirit also flagged, and the bandits grew ever bolder.
translations.idiomatic: The brave ones who pursued them covered thousands of li, but their spirit flagged as well, and the rebels grew ever bolder.

sentences.zh: 又經獻縣、交河，以薄滄州，滄州號有備，亦為所拔。

translations.literal: They passed again through Xian County and Jiaohe, pressing toward Cangzhou. Cangzhou was said to be well prepared, yet it too was taken.
translations.idiomatic: They passed again through Xian County and Jiaohe, pressing toward Cangzhou. Though Cangzhou was said to be well prepared, it too fell.

sentences.zh: 津地大震。

translations.literal: The Tianjin region was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin region was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊至梢直口，大吏不知所為，議嬰城守。

translations.literal: In the ninth month bandits reached Shaozhikou. High officials knew not what to do and debated holding the city firm under siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the rebels reached Shaozhikou. The senior officials were at a loss and debated simply holding the walls under siege.

sentences.zh: 子澄以負郭居民數十萬，不應棄之，力爭。

translations.literal: Zicheng argued that the hundreds of thousands of residents outside the walls should not be abandoned, and he contended forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng argued that the hundreds of thousands of residents outside the walls must not be abandoned, and he pressed the point forcefully.

sentences.zh: 遂用沿河棹小舟以火器取野鶩者，又火會會眾萬人，合水陸拒賊，而別向火會首事張錦文籌貲。

translations.literal: Thereupon they employed along the river those who rowed small boats and used firearms to hunt wild ducks. They also mobilized ten thousand men through the fire-society guild, combining land and water forces to resist bandits, while separately securing funds from Zhang Jinwen, head of the fire society.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they employed along the river duck hunters who rowed small boats armed with firearms. They also mustered ten thousand men through the fire-society guild, combining land and water forces to resist the rebels, while separately securing funds from Zhang Jinwen, head of the guild.

sentences.zh: 先是錦文輸家財濬壕，壕成，運河水大至，環城窪下成巨浸，而葡萄窪尤甚。

translations.literal: Earlier Jinwen had contributed family wealth to dredge moats. When the moats were completed, Grand Canal water rose greatly, and the low ground around the city became a vast flood, especially severe at Putao Wa.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jinwen had spent family wealth to dredge the moats. When they were done, Grand Canal water surged in, and the low ground around the city became a vast flood, deepest at Putao Wa.

sentences.zh: 子澄阻壕守，渡壕擊賊。

translations.literal: Zicheng defended behind the moat and crossed the moat to strike bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng held the line at the moat and crossed it to strike the rebels.

sentences.zh: 賊酋開山王小禿子手黃旗指揮，迅奮剽疾，能一躍丈餘，避槍擊。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Kaishan Wang Xiao Tuzi held a yellow flag in command. He was swift, fierce, and agile, able to leap more than a zhang in one bound and dodge gunfire.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain Kaishan Wang Xiao Tuzi commanded under a yellow flag. Swift, fierce, and agile, he could leap more than a zhang in one bound and dodge musket fire.

sentences.zh: 子澄先伏打野鴨船於岸外，賊以為民船也，呼渡，船槍發，殪小禿子，群賊奪氣。

translations.literal: Zicheng had first hidden duck-hunting boats offshore. The bandits took them for civilian boats and called to be ferried across. The boats fired their guns and killed Xiao Tuzi. The bandit host lost its spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng had hidden duck-hunting boats offshore. The rebels took them for civilian craft and called to be ferried across. The boats opened fire and killed Xiao Tuzi. The rebel host lost heart.

sentences.zh: 伏舟進擊餘賊，血流染波。

translations.literal: The hidden boats advanced to strike the remaining bandits. Blood stained the waves.
translations.idiomatic: The hidden boats advanced against the remaining rebels. Blood stained the waves.

sentences.zh: 日晡，軍餒，錦文又齎糗糧至，戰益奮。

translations.literal: By late afternoon the army was hungry. Jinwen again brought dried provisions, and the fighting grew ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the troops were hungry. Jinwen brought dried provisions again, and the fighting grew fiercer still.

sentences.zh: 勇目余鵬龍等相繼陷陣，复斬級無算，賊遁。

translations.literal: Militia squad leaders Yu Penglong and others fell in battle one after another. Again heads cut were beyond counting, and the bandits fled.
translations.idiomatic: Militia squad leaders Yu Penglong and others fell in battle one after another. Again the heads taken were beyond counting, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 是役也，子澄功最，旨以知府用，留本任。

translations.literal: In this battle Zicheng's merit was greatest. By imperial decree he was to be used as prefect but kept at his current post.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Zicheng's merit was greatest. By imperial decree he was to be appointed prefect but kept at his current post.

sentences.zh: 時賊退踞靜海及獨流鎮，子澄奉調赴勝保營，列營河西。

translations.literal: At the time the bandits withdrew to hold Jinghai and Duliuzhen. Zicheng received orders to proceed to Sheng Bao's camp and encamped west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the rebels withdrew to hold Jinghai and Duliuzhen. Zicheng was ordered to Sheng Bao's camp and encamped west of the river.

sentences.zh: 賊由獨流出撲，屢擊退之。

translations.literal: Bandits sallied from Duliuzhen in assault and were repeatedly driven back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied from Duliuzhen in assault and were repeatedly driven back.

sentences.zh: 嗣靜海賊傾巢出援，子澄追剿，賊竄，正窘，會都統佟鑑思絕賊歸路，進掣壕板，以路滑失足踣地，賊刃交下。

translations.literal: Then the bandits of Jinghai sent out their entire nest in relief. Zicheng pursued and suppressed them. The bandits scattered in flight and were in dire straits when, by chance, Banner general Tong Jian, seeking to cut the bandits' retreat, advanced and pulled up the plank over the moat. The road was slippery, he lost his footing and fell, and bandit blades struck from all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Jinghai rebels sent their entire force in relief. Zicheng pursued them. The rebels scattered and were in dire straits when, by chance, Banner general Tong Jian, seeking to cut their retreat, advanced and pulled up the plank over the moat. The road was slippery; he lost his footing and fell, and rebel blades struck from all sides.

sentences.zh: 子澄單騎馳救，砲洞馬腹，身受七傷。

translations.literal: Zicheng galloped alone to rescue him. A cannon ball pierced the horse's belly, and he himself received seven wounds.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng galloped alone to his rescue. A cannon ball pierced the horse's belly, and he himself received seven wounds.

sentences.zh: 鵬龍負之趨，子澄曰：「憊矣！

translations.literal: Penglong carried him as he fled. Zicheng said: "I am spent!
translations.idiomatic: Penglong carried him as he fled. Zicheng said: "I am spent!

sentences.zh: 爾亟行，毋顧我。」

translations.literal: You hurry away. Do not mind me."
translations.idiomatic: You must go at once. Do not mind me."

sentences.zh: 賊酋高剛頭薄之急，子澄恐為所辱，沉於河。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Gao Gangtou pressed close in haste. Zicheng feared being shamed by them and drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain Gao Gangtou pressed close. Fearing shame at their hands, Zicheng drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 鵬龍率從子陳樑等皆戰死。

translations.literal: Penglong, together with his adopted son Chen Liang and others, all died in battle.
