translations.idiomatic: He again purchased appointment as county assistant and was dispatched to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，署麻哈州吏目。

translations.literal: In the third month he held acting post as clerk of Mahe Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he served as acting clerk of Mahe Subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 四月，仁懷縣教匪楊漋喜竄麻哈，隨知州何鋌擊卻之。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the religious rebel Yang Zhangxi raided into Mahe. He followed Prefect He Ting in repelling them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the religious rebel Yang Zhangxi raided into Mahe. He followed Prefect He Ting in driving them back.

sentences.zh: 尋盜魁陳大陸糾苗匪來犯，复隨鋌出戰。

translations.literal: Soon the bandit chief Chen Dalu gathered Miao rebels to attack. Again he followed He Ting out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the bandit chief Chen Dalu gathered Miao rebels to attack. Again he followed He Ting into battle.

sentences.zh: 賊退，遂率眾攻拔下司岩、下雞場等處，扼茅坪山，悉力堵禦。

translations.literal: When the rebels retreated he then led the force to capture Xiasiyan, Xiajichang, and other places, held Maoping Mountain, and blocked with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels retreated he led troops to capture Xiasiyan, Xiajichang, and other places, seized Maoping Mountain, and blocked the enemy with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊聚益眾，勢不能敵。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels gathered in greater numbers and the force could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels gathered in greater numbers and the force could not hold against them.

sentences.zh: 退州城，賊旋陷都勻府。

translations.literal: They withdrew to the subprefecture city, and the rebels soon captured Duyun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They retreated to the subprefecture city, and the rebels soon captured Duyun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 提督孝順兵至茅坪被圍，寶錕率團兵隨總兵佟攀梅援剿，圍解。

translations.literal: When Regional Commander Xiaoshun's troops reached Maoping and were surrounded, Baokun led militia units following Brigade Commander Tong Panmei in relief and suppression, and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Regional Commander Xiaoshun's troops reached Maoping and were surrounded, Baokun led militia following Brigade Commander Tong Panmei in relief, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 自是無日不戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: From then on they fought every day, each side winning and losing in turn.
translations.idiomatic: From then on they fought every day, with victories and defeats on both sides.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蔣霨遠檄雲南降將陳得功隨孝順攻克都勻，進援麻哈，官軍勢復振。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Yunyuan ordered the Yunnan defector general Chen Degong to follow Xiaoshun in capturing Duyun and advancing to relieve Mahe, and government forces regained momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Yunyuan ordered the Yunnan defector general Chen Degong to follow Xiaoshun in recapturing Duyun and advancing to relieve Mahe, and government forces regained momentum.

sentences.zh: 得功旋叛去，孝順軍潰，賊大股圍州城三日，寶錕率鄉兵登陴固守，賊不​​得逞。

translations.literal: Degong soon rebelled and left. Xiaoshun's army collapsed. A large rebel force besieged the subprefecture city for three days. Baokun led local militia to mount the ramparts and hold firm, and the rebels could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Degong soon rebelled and departed. Xiaoshun's army collapsed. A large rebel force besieged the subprefecture city for three days. Baokun led local militia onto the ramparts and held firm, and the rebels could not break through.

sentences.zh: 七年，城中糧匱，兵益單，寶錕自誓與城存亡。

translations.literal: In the seventh year grain in the city ran short and troops grew fewer. Baokun swore to share the city's fate in life or death.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year provisions in the city ran short and troops grew fewer. Baokun vowed to live or die with the city.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，賊悉眾來攻，寶錕出北門迎敵，不利，入城，賊已自他門入。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year the rebels mustered all their forces to attack. Baokun went out the north gate to meet the enemy, fared badly, and entered the city, but the rebels had already entered through another gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year the rebels mustered all their forces to attack. Baokun went out the north gate to meet them, was driven back, and entered the city — but the rebels had already entered through another gate.

sentences.zh: 寶錕持矛巷戰，賊不忍害，揮令去。

translations.literal: Baokun fought with a spear in the alleys. The rebels could not bear to harm him and motioned for him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Baokun fought with a spear in the streets. The rebels could not bear to harm him and waved him away.

sentences.zh: 寶錕怒罵，掣矛刺之，賊奪矛還刺，死之。

translations.literal: Baokun cursed in rage, pulled back his spear to thrust at them, and the rebels seized the spear and stabbed him back, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Baokun cursed in fury and thrust at them with his spear. The rebels seized the spear, stabbed him in return, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 王汝揆，甘肅伏羌人。

translations.literal: Wang Rukui was a native of Fuxiang, Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rukui was a native of Fuxiang in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 道光二十年舉人，揀選知縣，親老改教職。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of the twentieth year of Daoguang, selected for magistrate, he changed to an educational post because his parents were elderly.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate in the twentieth year of Daoguang, he was selected for magistrate but changed to an educational post because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 咸豐間，授平涼縣教諭。

translations.literal: During the Xianfeng period he received appointment as instructor of Pingliang County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng period he was appointed instructor of Pingliang County.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，陝西回匪竄乾鳳，偪甘肅境，汝揆上書平慶涇道萬金鏞曰：「賊西偪鳳翔，必分黨由汧、隴間道趨秦安東北，構煽醜類。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Shaanxi Muslim rebels raided into Qian and Feng and pressed the Gansu border, Rukui wrote to Wan Jinyong, intendant of the Ping-Qing-Jing Circuit, saying: 'The rebels pressing west toward Fengxiang will certainly send a party by the secret routes through Qian and Long to strike the northeast of Qin'an and stir up the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Shaanxi Muslim rebels raided into Qian and Feng and pressed the Gansu border, Rukui wrote to Wan Jinyong, intendant of the Ping-Qing-Jing Circuit, saying: 'The rebels pressing west toward Fengxiang will certainly send a detachment by the secret routes through Qian and Long to strike northeast Qin'an and incite the wicked.

sentences.zh: 宜及其未至，扼險嚴防。

translations.literal: It is best to seize the passes and defend strictly before they arrive.
translations.idiomatic: We should seize the passes and defend them strictly before they arrive.

sentences.zh: 不然，內應且四起，平涼擾則靈、固、狄、河等州縣亦危矣！」

translations.literal: Otherwise internal collaborators will rise on every side. If Pingliang is disturbed, then the prefectures and counties of Ling, Gu, Di, He, and others will also be in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise collaborators within will rise on every side. If Pingliang is thrown into turmoil, the prefectures and counties of Ling, Gu, Di, He, and others will also be endangered!

sentences.zh: 言未及用，賊尋由固關逾隴，張家川、蓮花城土回應之，陷鹽茶及固原，金鏞死之，平涼戒嚴。

translations.literal: Before his words could be acted upon, the rebels soon crossed Long from Guyuan Pass. Local Muslims at Zhangjiachuan and Lianhuacheng responded, and Yan Cha and Guyuan fell. Jin Yong died, and Pingliang was placed under martial alert.
translations.idiomatic: Before his advice could be acted on, the rebels crossed Long from Guyuan Pass. Local Muslims at Zhangjiachuan and Lianhuacheng rose in response, Yan Cha and Guyuan fell, Jin Yong was killed, and Pingliang was placed under martial alert.

sentences.zh: 汝揆議盡毀城外民舍，無令賊倚為障蔽，議不行。

translations.literal: Rukui proposed destroying all civilian dwellings outside the city walls so the rebels could not use them as cover. The proposal was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui proposed tearing down all dwellings outside the walls so the rebels could not use them as cover. The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊圍平涼，汝揆協同守令，督率生徒，登陴固守，衣不解帶者六閱月。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels besieged Pingliang. Rukui cooperated with the defending officials, supervised and led the students, mounted the ramparts to hold firm, and for six months did not remove his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels besieged Pingliang. Rukui worked with the defending officials, led his students onto the ramparts, and held the walls for six months without removing his clothes.

sentences.zh: 一日，偵西北二路賊少可擊，謁知府田增壽請率壯士縋城出剿，又不許。

translations.literal: One day, reconnaissance showed the rebels on the northwest and north routes were few enough to attack. He visited Prefect Tian Zengshou and requested to lead stalwart men lowered by rope from the walls to suppress them, but again permission was denied.
translations.idiomatic: One day scouts reported that rebel forces on the northwest and north routes were thin enough to attack. He petitioned Prefect Tian Zengshou to lead stalwart men out over the walls by rope to strike them, but permission was again denied.

sentences.zh: 二年，賊匿民舍掘地道，納火藥轟之，城遂陷。

translations.literal: In the second year the rebels hid in civilian dwellings and dug tunnels, loaded gunpowder, and blasted the walls, and the city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the rebels hid in civilian dwellings, dug tunnels, packed them with gunpowder, and blasted the walls, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 人皆泣曰：「早從教諭言，事豈至此乎？」

translations.literal: Everyone wept and said: 'Had we followed the instructor's advice earlier, how could matters have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wept and said: 'Had we heeded the instructor's advice sooner, how could things have come to this?

sentences.zh: 汝揆還署，易朝服，北向叩首訖，妻汪氏暨女一、孫女一皆死，乃從容就縊於孔廟鍾虡以殉。

translations.literal: Rukui returned to his office, changed into court robes, kowtowed toward the north until finished. His wife Lady Wang together with one daughter and one granddaughter all died. Then he calmly went to hang himself at the bell frame in the Confucian temple to die with them.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui returned to his office, changed into court robes, and kowtowed toward the north. His wife Lady Wang, one daughter, and one granddaughter all died first. Then he calmly hanged himself at the bell frame in the Confucian temple to join them in death.

sentences.zh: 汝揆性質實，敦孝友。

translations.literal: Rukui's nature was honest and solid, and he was devoted in filial piety and brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Rukui was honest and steadfast by nature, and devoted in filial piety and brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，不入內，不御酒肉。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his parents he did not enter the inner quarters and did not partake of wine or meat.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his parents he did not enter the inner quarters and abstained from wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 弟印揆，客西寧久，音信乏絕，汝揆往尋之，風雪中徒步千餘裡，卒挈其弟以歸。

translations.literal: His younger brother Yinkui had long been a guest in Xining with no word received. Rukui went to seek him, walking more than a thousand li on foot through wind and snow, and at last brought his brother home.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yinkui had long been in Xining with no word from him. Rukui went to find him, walking more than a thousand li on foot through wind and snow, and at last brought his brother home.

sentences.zh: 平生肆力於經籍，家居課徒，以窮經為急，輒點勘善本授之，勗以立品敦行。

translations.literal: All his life he devoted himself to the classics. At home he taught disciples, making mastery of the classics urgent, and would collate fine editions to give them, urging them to establish character and cultivate conduct.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he devoted himself to the classics. At home he taught disciples with mastering the classics as his priority, collating fine editions for them and urging them to build character and live uprightly.

sentences.zh: 其官平涼，亦以是為教。

translations.literal: When he served at Pingliang he also made this his teaching.
translations.idiomatic: In his post at Pingliang he taught the same way.

sentences.zh: 期年，訟庭無士子跡。

translations.literal: Within a year there were no scholars' traces in the litigation court.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year no scholar appeared in the litigation court.

sentences.zh: 當城未陷之先兩月，有門人馳書勸引疾歸，謂可免難。

translations.literal: Two months before the city fell, a disciple sent a hurried letter urging him to plead illness and return home, saying he could thus escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Two months before the city fell, a disciple sent an urgent letter urging him to plead illness and return home, saying he could escape the disaster that way.

sentences.zh: 汝揆曰：「無疾而稱疾，是欺也；

translations.literal: Rukui said: 'To claim illness when there is none — that is deception;
translations.idiomatic: Rukui said: 'To claim illness when there is none is deception;

sentences.zh: 食祿而苟免，非義也。」

translations.literal: to receive salary and seek escape — that is not righteous.
translations.idiomatic: to draw salary and seek escape is not righteous.

sentences.zh: 乃為書與戚友訣，略曰：「我生不辰，逢天癉怒，向者耳聞之，今則目睹之。

translations.literal: He then wrote letters of farewell to kin and friends, saying in brief: 'I was born at an unlucky hour and met Heaven's wrathful scourge. What I once heard of, I now see with my own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote farewell letters to kin and friends, saying in brief: 'I was born at an unlucky hour and met Heaven's wrathful scourge. What I once heard of, I now see with my own eyes.

sentences.zh: 平郡自二月以來，圍困日迫，飛書告急，援兵無一至者。

translations.literal: Ping Prefecture since the second month has been besieged with the crisis pressing daily. Urgent dispatches pleaded for relief, yet not one relief force arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Prefecture has been besieged since the second month, the crisis pressing daily. Urgent dispatches pleaded for relief, yet not one relief force arrived.

sentences.zh: 汝揆妻、女，行當自盡，決不受辱於賊手。

translations.literal: Rukui's wife and daughter will soon take their own lives, resolved never to suffer dishonor at rebel hands.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and daughter will soon take their own lives, resolved never to suffer dishonor at rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 死者士之終，今誠獲死所矣。

translations.literal: Death is the scholar's end; today I truly obtain a place to die.
translations.idiomatic: Death is the scholar's end; today I truly find a place worthy to die.

sentences.zh: 惟官卑不得展一籌以報國，死有餘憾耳。」

translations.literal: Only because my office was low I could not deploy one stratagem to repay the state — in death I still have regret.
translations.idiomatic: Only because my rank was low I could not offer one stratagem to repay the state — in death I still have regret.

sentences.zh: 三年，官軍克平涼，總督楊岳斌請優恤。

translations.literal: In the third year government troops recovered Pingliang. Governor-General Yang Yuebin requested exceptional mourning honors.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year government troops recaptured Pingliang. Governor-General Yang Yuebin requested exceptional mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 六年，總督穆圖善疏陳汝揆死事狀，請照陣亡例議卹，贈國子監助教銜，給世職，又命於本籍建祠，以從死之妻、女等附祀。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Governor-General Mutu Shan memorialized the circumstances of Rukui's death, requesting mourning deliberation according to the precedent for death in battle. He was posthumously granted the rank of National University assistant instructor, awarded a hereditary office, and ordered that a shrine be built in his native place with his wife, daughter, and others who died with him enshrined there.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Governor-General Mutu Shan memorialized the circumstances of Rukui's death and requested mourning honors under the precedent for death in battle. He was posthumously granted the rank of National University assistant instructor, awarded a hereditary office, and a shrine was ordered in his native place with his wife, daughter, and others who died with him enshrined there.
